EntityResolution+DependencyAnalysis+LargeGraphInference ... engineering/scaling challenges. A normal PC can execute the fundamental mechanisms
rationale_evidence.statement: Lists the layer's computational primitives as normal-PC computable, with entity resolution + dependency analysis + large graph inference identified as the scaling-challenge frontier rather than a theoretical barrier.

sources.note: S0907's Step 25N: the fully worked statistical/qualitative evidence-aggregation model (likelihood ratios, evidence clusters, authority-vs-reliability separation, no-universal-aggregation-function conclusion); extends B0021's evidence-aggregation-axioms (S0859) and S0892's evidence-aggregation-algebra (B0021) with a concrete operator, DDD service mapping, and eight falsification tests.

rows.anchor: E=(Content,Source,Provenance,Method,Time,Context,Reliability,Independence,Authority,Uncertainty) ... 0.87+0.76+0.91 has no generally valid statistical interpretation
rows.statement: Rejects representing evidence as a bare scalar confidence summed across items (0.87+0.76+0.91 has no valid statistical interpretation), proposing instead a ten-field Evidence tuple E=(Content,Source,Provenance,Method,Time,Context,Reliability,Independence,Authority,Uncertainty), not all fields required per domain.

rows.anchor: Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence ... they answer different questions
rows.statement: States six concepts that must remain separate: Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence — each answers a different question.

rows.anchor: Support(E,A) ... Supports/Contradicts/Neutral/Undetermined ... can be deterministic
rows.statement: Defines Support(E,A) with four possible values (Supports, Contradicts, Neutral, Undetermined), potentially deterministic.

rows.anchor: Reliability(E,A,C) ... Production API high reliability for current version, Human memory low reliability for exact historical version ... context-dependent
rows.statement: Defines Reliability(E,A,C) as context-dependent trustworthiness of a source/method for a specific claim type, illustrated with production-API-vs-human-memory example.

rows.anchor: A production server may be authoritative for CurrentInstalledVersion ... an Architecture Board ... ArchitectureApproval ... Authority\neq Reliability
rows.statement: Defines Authority as organizational/legal standing to establish or approve an assertion, distinct from Reliability, worked with a production-server-vs-Architecture-Board example.

rows.anchor: An engineer says Nexus 3.70 is approved ... Authority(engineer,ArchitectureApproval)=False ... exactly the type of distinction a governance-aware KnowledgeOS needs
rows.statement: Worked example: a technically reliable engineer's approval statement is Authority(engineer,ArchitectureApproval)=False since only the Architecture Board can authorize — technically useful evidence can be insufficient for authoritative approval.

rows.anchor: P(H\mid E) ... not Reliability(E), nor Authority(E), nor Confidence(E)
rows.statement: Defines Probability P(H|E) as uncertainty under an explicit probabilistic model, distinct from Reliability, Authority, and Confidence.

rows.anchor: Confidence is unfortunately overloaded ... Confidence=(value,model,interpretation)
rows.statement: Notes 'confidence' is overloaded (subjective/model/statistical-level/probability/classifier-score) and should never be stored as a bare number without a ConfidenceModel; proposes Confidence=(value,model,interpretation) if used at all.

rows.anchor: E_1 and E_2 both support H. We cannot simply assume E_1\perp E_2 ... need to examine their causal/provenance relationship
rows.statement: States Independence as the most important statistical dimension: co-supporting evidence cannot be assumed independent without examining causal/provenance relationships.

rows.anchor: Vendor document -> Human summary / LLM summary ... E_2=f(E_1), E_3=g(E_1) ... EvidenceCount\neq InformationCount
rows.statement: Worked classic double-counting example: human and LLM summaries both derived from one vendor document are not independent observations — counting them as three sources falsely inflates support — 'EvidenceCount ≠ InformationCount,' called 'a fundamental principle.'

rows.anchor: G_E=(V,E) ... nodes are evidence/artifacts and edges represent derivation/dependency ... allows us to detect obvious double-counting
rows.statement: Proposes an evidence lineage graph G_E=(V,E) with nodes as evidence/artifacts and edges as derivation/dependency, illustrated with a vendor-document/human-extract/LLM-extract/assertion diagram, enabling double-counting detection.

rows.anchor: EvidenceClusters ... C_1=\{VendorDocument,HumanSummary,LLMSummary\} ... InformationUnits(C_1)\approx1 unless additional independent observations exist
rows.statement: Defines EvidenceClusters grouping evidence sharing a common informational origin; a cluster contributes InformationUnits≈1 unless additional independent observations exist.

rows.anchor: Production API->E1, Filesystem inspection->E2, Independent human inspection->E3 ... E_1\perp E_2 may be justified ... based on the actual acquisition mechanism, not simply they came from different people
rows.statement: Contrasts genuinely independent acquisition paths (API, filesystem inspection, independent human inspection), warning independence must be justified by acquisition mechanism, not merely 'different people.'

rows.anchor: E_1\perp E_2\mid H ... ConditionalIndependence(E_1,E_2\mid H,C) ... should not force everything into simple binary independence
rows.statement: Introduces conditional independence E1⊥E2|H, generalized to ConditionalIndependence(E1,E2|H,C), avoiding forcing evidence into simple binary independence.

rows.anchor: Polarity(E,H)\in\{Positive,Negative,Neutral,Unknown\} ... a useful deterministic layer before probabilistic aggregation
rows.statement: Defines evidence Polarity(E,H) in {Positive,Negative,Neutral,Unknown}, a deterministic layer applied before any probabilistic aggregation.

rows.anchor: Strength(E,H) ... LikelihoodRatio\gg1 ... LikelihoodRatio\approx1 ... statistically meaningful measure of evidential strength may be a likelihood ratio, not a subjective score
rows.statement: Argues evidential Strength(E,H) is best captured by a likelihood ratio rather than a subjective score, contrasting strong (LR>>1) vs weak (LR≈1) measurements.

rows.anchor: LR(E)=\frac{P(E\mid H)}{P(E\mid\neg H)} ... LR>1 favors H, LR<1 favors \neg H, LR\approx1 little discrimination ... much more principled than Confidence=0.8
rows.statement: Formally defines the likelihood ratio LR(E)=P(E|H)/P(E|¬H) with a three-way interpretation (favors H, favors ¬H, uninformative), 'much more principled than Confidence=0.8.'

rows.anchor: LR(E_1,E_2)=LR(E_1)\cdot LR(E_2) ... LR(E_1,\ldots,E_n)=\prod_i LR(E_i) under the appropriate independence assumptions
rows.statement: Defines combination of conditionally independent evidence via multiplied likelihood ratios: LR(E1,...,En)=prod LR(Ei), 'a mathematically valid evidence-combination mechanism.'

rows.anchor: No independence assumption without provenance/model justification
rows.statement: States the strict invariant that the LR product formula must never be applied automatically without provenance/model justification for E_i⊥E_j|H — otherwise 'severe overconfidence' results.

rows.anchor: Odds(H)=P(H)/(1-P(H)) ... Odds(H\mid E)=Odds(H)\times LR(E) ... requires a valid prior; valid likelihoods; a valid dependency model. Without those, we should not fabricate probabilities
rows.statement: Defines Bayesian odds updating Odds(H|E)=Odds(H)*LR(E), generalized to independent multi-evidence updating, with an explicit requirement for a valid prior/likelihoods/dependency model — otherwise probabilities must not be fabricated.

rows.anchor: SupportState(A)=Strong,Moderate,Weak,Conflicted,Insufficient ... must be defined by the relevant epistemic contract
rows.statement: Defines a qualitative SupportState alternative (Strong, Moderate, Weak, Conflicted, Insufficient) for the normal enterprise case lacking a valid probability model, with categories defined by the epistemic contract.

rows.anchor: Regime A Statistical P(H\mid E) ... Regime B Qualitative SupportState(H) ... Both are legitimate ... QualitativeSupport\neq Probability
rows.statement: Defines two legitimate aggregation regimes (Statistical, Qualitative), warning against silently mixing them (Strong=0.8 or Probability=0.8=>Strong only if explicitly organization-defined) — QualitativeSupport ≠ Probability.

rows.anchor: E_1: Engineer says approved ... E_2: Architecture Board decision says approved ... AuthorityFilter(A) ... EvidenceSupport does not imply GovernanceAuthority
rows.statement: Worked example: even if the engineer's statement has higher technical reliability, the Architecture Board's decision may be authoritative — an AuthorityFilter can dominate — 'EvidenceSupport does not imply GovernanceAuthority.'

rows.anchor: Aggregate(E_1,\ldots,E_n,A): 1. Identify evidence ... 10. Produce aggregate assessment ... much safer than simply averaging scores
rows.statement: Presents a ten-step Aggregate(E1..En,A) pipeline (identify evidence; verify provenance; determine dependency/independence; determine polarity; determine applicability; assess reliability; assess authority; apply statistical/qualitative model; detect contradiction; produce aggregate assessment) — 'much safer than simply averaging scores.'

rows.anchor: Assertion: NexusVersion=3.69, Support: Strong, Evidence: E17,E21,E44, IndependentEvidenceClusters: 3, ContradictingEvidence: none, Authority: sufficient, AssessmentModel: InfrastructureEvidencePolicy v2, Probability: not calculated
rows.statement: Gives a worked structured qualitative aggregate-assessment output (assertion, support level, contributing evidence, independent-cluster count, contradicting evidence, authority sufficiency, assessment model version, probability status) as 'much more meaningful' than a bare confidence number.

rows.anchor: Hypothesis H, Prior: specified by model, Evidence: E1,E2,E3, Posterior: P(H|E1,E2,E3)=..., IndependenceModel: specified, Sensitivity: ... ... Now the probability is interpretable
rows.statement: Gives a worked structured statistical aggregate-assessment output when a legitimate probabilistic model exists, including prior, evidence, posterior, independence model, and sensitivity — making 'the probability... interpretable.'

rows.anchor: P(H\mid E)=0.96 ... Prior\in[0.2,0.8] ... if the conclusion remains stable across the interval, the conclusion is robust. If it changes dramatically, the assessment is fragile
rows.statement: Introduces sensitivity/robustness analysis: testing conclusion stability across a plausible prior range (e.g. [0.2,0.8]) distinguishes a robust conclusion from a fragile one, conceptually related to a partial derivative of P(H|E) with respect to Prior.

rows.anchor: Sarathi should not merely see P(H)=0.96. It should potentially see Robustness(H) ... DecisionQuality depends on robustness, not only point estimate
rows.statement: Argues Sarathi should see Robustness(H), not merely a point-estimate probability, since a decision at 0.96 that collapses to 0.55 under plausible assumptions differs meaningfully from one stable above 0.95 across all plausible models — 'DecisionQuality depends on robustness, not only point estimate.'

rows.anchor: Strong positive+weak negative: Support(H)=Strong ... Strong+strong: Support(H)=Conflicted ... unknown relative strength: Unresolved ... should not arbitrarily cancel them: +1-1=0
rows.statement: Classifies conflicting-evidence scenarios into three outcomes (Strong, Conflicted, Unresolved) depending on relative strength, explicitly rejecting naive polarity cancellation (+1-1=0) as 'generally meaningless.'

rows.anchor: System telemetry says Version=3.70, Manual note says Version=3.69 ... not because Telemetry=3.70 is mathematically more true. It is because the epistemic model gives it stronger evidential characteristics
rows.statement: Worked example: preferring current telemetry over a manual note is a consequence of the evidential model's characteristics (currency, directness), not a claim of greater metaphysical truth.

rows.anchor: Even when E_1 is authoritative, the conflicting E_2 should remain recorded ... ConflictHistory is preserved ... E_1 dominates E_2. but E_2 is not deleted
rows.statement: States authority-resolved conflicts must not erase the dominated evidence: ConflictHistory is preserved, current assessment records 'E1 dominates E2' without deleting E2.

rows.anchor: \mathcal A(E_1,\ldots,E_n;A,M)\rightarrow Assessment(A) ... no universal evidence aggregation function
rows.statement: Defines the abstract aggregation operator A(E1,...,En;A,M) -> Assessment(A), deliberately model-dependent — 'there is no universal evidence aggregation function... an important mathematical conclusion.'

rows.anchor: Authority=High but Reliability=Low ... Authority=Low but Reliability=High ... no universal mathematical answer ... depends on Question, Domain, Contract, Governance
rows.statement: Worked counterexample showing why no universal aggregation function exists: a high-authority/low-reliability source versus a low-authority/high-reliability source has no universal winner — depends on Question, Domain, Contract, Governance — 'EvidenceAggregation is domain/model dependent.'

rows.anchor: EvidenceAssessmentService inside an appropriate bounded context ... should not be embedded into the generic Evidence Entity
rows.statement: Maps evidence aggregation onto DDD as a dedicated EvidenceAssessmentService domain service inside an appropriate bounded context, kept separate from the generic Evidence entity (which stores only provenance/source/content/context/timestamps).

rows.anchor: Support(E,A_1)\neq Support(E,A_2) ... evidence has no universal support value independent of the assertion
rows.statement: Worked example: the same version evidence is strong for 'what version is installed?' but irrelevant for 'is the migration approved?' — Support(E,A1) ≠ Support(E,A2), evidence has no universal support value independent of the assertion.

rows.anchor: Relevance(E,A,C)\in\{Relevant,Irrelevant,Unknown\} ... should occur before aggregation
rows.statement: Defines Relevance(E,A,C) in {Relevant,Irrelevant,Unknown} as a pre-aggregation gate.

rows.anchor: Relevant=True but Applicable=False ... demonstrates why context must be explicit ... Applicable(E,A,t) must include time
rows.statement: Distinguishes Relevance from Applicability: a Development-system version fact is relevant to a version-question but not Applicable to a Production assertion (Relevant=True, Applicable=False); also requires temporal applicability Applicable(E,A,t).

rows.anchor: Evidence->Identity->Provenance->Dependency Analysis->Relevance->Applicability->Polarity->Reliability->Authority->Statistical/Qualitative Model->Conflict Analysis->Aggregate Assessment->Knowledge State ... a robust architecture
rows.statement: Presents the final consolidated evidence-aggregation pipeline diagram spanning thirteen stages from raw Evidence to Knowledge State — 'a robust architecture.'

rows.anchor: Test A duplicate: InformationGain=0. Test B derived duplicate: IndependentSupport(E2)=0 unless genuinely new information. Test C independent corroboration: Support(H) increases. Test D contradictory: Conflict(H). Test E irrelevant: Support=0/Irrelevant. Test F stale: CurrentApplicability=False, hist
rows.statement: Runs eight falsification tests (A-H, all PASS) against the evidence-aggregation model: exact duplicate yields zero information gain; a derived duplicate yields zero independent support unless genuinely new information is introduced; independently-corroborating evidence increases support; contradictory evidence yields Conflict(H); irrelevant evidence yields zero/irrelevant support; stale evidence yields CurrentApplicability=False while historical validity remains; an authority mismatch keeps Support and Authority distinct; and, given valid likelihoods and independence assumptions, a posterior can be computed.

experiment.hypothesis: The evidence-aggregation model (dependency, relevance, applicability, authority, statistical combination) behaves correctly across eight representative scenarios.
experiment.setup: Eight scenarios A-H: duplicate, derived duplicate, independent corroboration, contradiction, irrelevance, staleness, authority mismatch, valid probabilistic model.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.method: apply the aggregation pipeline/operator to each scenario
experiment.result: All eight scenarios produce the theoretically expected assessment
experiment.interpretation: Confirms the aggregation model avoids double-counting, false conflation, and unjustified overconfidence across the tested cases.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeStrength=NumberOfEvidenceItems ... formally reject ... KnowledgeAssessment=f(Evidence,Provenance,Dependency,Relevance,Applicability,Reliability,Authority,Model)
rows.statement: Formally rejects KnowledgeStrength=NumberOfEvidenceItems, replacing it with KnowledgeAssessment as a function of Evidence, Provenance, Dependency, Relevance, Applicability, Reliability, Authority, and Model — 'a much stronger foundation.'

rows.anchor: do not know the dependency structure ... assume independence? maximum correlation? conservative bounds? represent the uncertainty explicitly? ask for additional evidence? There is no universal answer
rows.statement: Identifies the genuinely unresolved statistical question of unknown dependency structure among evidence items, listing five candidate strategies (assume independence, assume maximum correlation, conservative bounds, represent uncertainty explicitly, seek additional evidence) with no universal answer — 'where robust statistics and uncertainty modeling enter.'

rows.anchor: Do not claim more evidential strength than the dependency model justifies ... Independence=Unknown ... should not calculate LR_{combined}=LR_1LR_2LR_3 as if independence were established
rows.statement: States the Conservative Evidence Principle default for high-stakes decisions: never claim more evidential strength than the dependency model justifies — if independence is unknown, the LR product must not be computed as though it were established — 'a strong safety invariant.'

rows.anchor: Aggregate assessment: unresolved ... Recommended next action: obtain independent observation ... Zero contains NeedIndependentEvidence ... Lord can select an action to acquire it
rows.statement: Argues evidence aggregation need not always produce a number — a legitimate result can be 'unresolved' with a recommended next action, feeding Zero's NeedIndependentEvidence and letting Lord select an acquisition action — 'elegantly reconnects the statistical layer to the Lord loop.'

rows.anchor: Evidence->Assessment->Knowledge ... Assessment->Zero->Lord->NewObservation->Evidence ... genuinely closed-loop epistemic reasoning
rows.statement: Summarizes the complete epistemic feedback loop: Evidence->Assessment->Knowledge normally, with Assessment->Zero->Lord->NewObservation->Evidence when assessment is insufficient — 'genuinely closed-loop epistemic reasoning.'

rows.anchor: 25N — PASS ... Universal evidence weight [not universally computable] ... no single mathematically correct number ... independently of Claim+Context+Model
rows.statement: Step 25N self-verdict: PASS, with a proven/computable list (identity, provenance, dependency, relevance, applicability, polarity, reliability/authority representation, contradiction, qualitative/probabilistic aggregation, uncertainty representation) versus one explicitly not universally computable item: Universal evidence weight — no single number represents evidential strength independent of Claim+Context+Model.

rows.anchor: Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight. Its epistemic effect is relational: Effect(E,A\mid C,M)
rows.statement: States the major result for the whole architecture: evidence has no intrinsic universal weight; its epistemic effect is relational, Effect(E,A|C,M) — 'a very important principle.'

rows.anchor: What exactly is truth inside KnowledgeOS? ... WorldTruth, ObservedTruth, LogicalTruth, SupportedAssertion, ProbableAssertion, GovernanceTruth, Unknown ... Step 25O
rows.statement: Closes by posing the truth/validity question and naming seven concepts to formalize (WorldTruth, ObservedTruth, LogicalTruth, SupportedAssertion, ProbableAssertion, GovernanceTruth, Unknown), transitioning into Step 25O — the same content already processed earlier in this batch as S0906, confirming the file-order deviation from the theory's own step numbering.

lineage_claims.target: Step 25O (S0906, processed earlier in this batch)
lineage_claims.quote: Step 25O — Truth, Validity, Belief, Knowledge and the Epistemic Status of an Assertion

lexical.anchor: E=(Content,Source,Provenance,Method,Time,Context,Reliability,Independence,Authority,Uncertainty) ... 0.87+0.76+0.91 has no generally valid statistical interpretation

conceptual.anchor: EvidenceAssessmentService inside an appropriate bounded context ... should not be embedded into the generic Evidence Entity

formal.anchor: E=(Content,Source,Provenance,Method,Time,Context,Reliability,Independence,Authority,Uncertainty) ... 0.87+0.76+0.91 has no generally valid statistical interpretation

operational.anchor: Test A duplicate: InformationGain=0. Test B derived duplicate: IndependentSupport(E2)=0 unless genuinely new information. Test C independent corroboration: Support(H) increases. Test D contradictory: Conflict(H). Test E irrelevant: Support=0/Irrelevant. Test F stale: CurrentApplicability=False, hist

rationale_evidence.anchor: Strength(E,H) ... LikelihoodRatio\gg1 ... LikelihoodRatio\approx1 ... statistically meaningful measure of evidential strength may be a likelihood ratio, not a subjective score
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues evidential Strength(E,H) is best captured by a likelihood ratio rather than a subjective score, contrasting strong (LR>>1) vs weak (LR≈1) measurements.

rationale_evidence.anchor: SupportState(A)=Strong,Moderate,Weak,Conflicted,Insufficient ... must be defined by the relevant epistemic contract
rationale_evidence.statement: Defines a qualitative SupportState alternative (Strong, Moderate, Weak, Conflicted, Insufficient) for the normal enterprise case lacking a valid probability model, with categories defined by the epistemic contract.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Aggregate(E_1,\ldots,E_n,A): 1. Identify evidence ... 10. Produce aggregate assessment ... much safer than simply averaging scores
rationale_evidence.statement: Presents a ten-step Aggregate(E1..En,A) pipeline (identify evidence; verify provenance; determine dependency/independence; determine polarity; determine applicability; assess reliability; assess authority; apply statistical/qualitative model; detect contradiction; produce aggregate assessment) — 'much safer than simply averaging scores.'

rationale_evidence.anchor: P(H\mid E)=0.96 ... Prior\in[0.2,0.8] ... if the conclusion remains stable across the interval, the conclusion is robust. If it changes dramatically, the assessment is fragile
rationale_evidence.statement: Introduces sensitivity/robustness analysis: testing conclusion stability across a plausible prior range (e.g. [0.2,0.8]) distinguishes a robust conclusion from a fragile one, conceptually related to a partial derivative of P(H|E) with respect to Prior.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Authority=High but Reliability=Low ... Authority=Low but Reliability=High ... no universal mathematical answer ... depends on Question, Domain, Contract, Governance
rationale_evidence.statement: Worked counterexample showing why no universal aggregation function exists: a high-authority/low-reliability source versus a low-authority/high-reliability source has no universal winner — depends on Question, Domain, Contract, Governance — 'EvidenceAggregation is domain/model dependent.'

aliases: Decision Theory, Utility, Risk, Value of Information and Rational Action

sources.note: S0910's Step 25R: the formal Value-of-Information theory giving Zero and Lord's information-acquisition behavior a rigorous decision-theoretic foundation; extends formal-sarathi-decision-algebra (S0900) and formal-lord-action-selection-algebra (S0899) with EU, tail risk, VOI, regret, and robustness.

rows.anchor: most probable outcome\Rightarrow best action ... mathematically wrong in general ... Knowledge\rightarrow Prediction\rightarrow Consequences\rightarrow Utility/Risk\rightarrow Decision
rows.statement: Rejects the implicit assumption 'most probable outcome => best action' as mathematically wrong in general, establishing the correct chain Knowledge->Prediction->Consequences->Utility/Risk->Decision, plus a Decision<->ValueOfInformation relationship.

rows.anchor: Decision is not inference ... S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\} ... A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\} ... decision theory evaluates a\in A under uncertainty about s\in S
rows.statement: Distinguishes inference ('what do we believe?') from decision ('what should we do?'), formalizing state space S and action space A.

rows.anchor: U(a,s) ... EU(a\mid E)=\sum_s P(s\mid E)U(a,s) ... a^*=\arg\max_a EU(a\mid E)
rows.statement: Defines utility U(a,s), expected utility EU(a|E)=sum_s P(s|E)U(a,s), and the rational-choice rule a*=argmax_a EU(a|E).

rows.anchor: P(Outage\mid Upgrade)=0.05 ... tells us almost nothing ... U(Upgrade,Outage) and U(DoNothing,Outage) ... the decision emerges from the whole consequence structure
rows.statement: Worked example/table showing a bare 5% outage probability tells almost nothing about whether to upgrade absent the full action/outcome/consequence structure.

rows.anchor: Risk=Probability ... ExpectedLoss=\sum_s P(s\mid E)L(a,s) ... real risk can involve multiple outcomes; uncertainty intervals; catastrophic tails; irreversibility; regulatory consequences; opportunity costs
rows.statement: Rejects reducing Risk to Probability, defining ExpectedLoss=sum_s P(s|E)L(a,s) and listing six additional real-risk dimensions beyond a single probability number.

rows.anchor: Action A: P(Loss=10000)=0.10 ... Action B: P(Loss=1000000)=0.001 ... same expected loss ... TailRisk is dramatically larger ... ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient
rows.statement: Worked tail-risk example: two actions with identical expected loss (1000) but vastly different catastrophic-tail severity may be rationally treated differently — 'ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient'; risk policy must specify how severe/irreversible outcomes are treated.

rows.anchor: U(\euro x)=\sqrt{x} ... UtilityFunction is a normative choice. KnowledgeOS should not secretly invent one
rows.statement: Notes utility functions (e.g. sqrt(x)) can encode risk aversion but are a normative organizational choice that KnowledgeOS must not secretly invent.

rows.anchor: DecisionContract=(Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) ... a very important DDD concept
rows.statement: Defines a seven-field DecisionContract (Actions,States,UtilityModel,Constraints,RiskPolicy,Authority,EvidenceRequirements) as an important DDD concept.

rows.anchor: EU(a_1)>EU(a_2) but Authorized(a_1)=False ... a^*=\arg\max_{a\in A_{admissible}}EU(a) ... Optimization occurs within admissible actions
rows.statement: States optimization occurs within admissible actions only: an unauthorized highest-utility action must not execute — a*=argmax over A_admissible, not all of A.

rows.anchor: TechnicalRiskTooHigh or GovernanceAuthorizationMissing or EvidenceInsufficient ... DecisionStatus: blocked, Reason: governance_authorization_missing
rows.statement: Requires Sarathi to distinguish blocking-failure reasons (technical risk, governance authorization missing, evidence insufficient) via a structured DecisionStatus=blocked+Reason record, rather than a bare 'decision=no.'

rows.anchor: a^*=Upgrade [recommendation] ... does not necessarily mean Decision=Approved ... Recommendation\neq Decision\neq Authorization
rows.statement: States Recommendation ≠ Decision ≠ Authorization: an AI-computed optimum is only a Recommendation until an authorized human/body decides.

rows.anchor: Sarathi as a decision-support/decision-orchestration intelligence, not as an autonomous source of authority ... Sarathi:(K,Models,Constraints)\rightarrow DecisionCandidate ... Authorize(DecisionCandidate)
rows.statement: Characterizes Sarathi as decision-support/orchestration intelligence producing a DecisionCandidate, with governance separately determining Authorize(DecisionCandidate).

rows.anchor: Lord may choose between Action and InformationAcquisition ... Option 1 make decision now ... Option 4 ask human expert ... the system therefore performs meta-decision-making
rows.statement: Formalizes Lord's role as choosing between Action and InformationAcquisition, worked with a four-option example (decide now, collect observation, run simulation, ask human expert) — 'the system performs meta-decision-making.'

rows.anchor: VOI=EU(\text{best decision after information})-EU(\text{best decision now}) ... VOI(E)=E_e[\max_a EU(a\mid E,e)]-\max_a EU(a\mid E) ... one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture
rows.statement: Formally defines Value of Information via two equivalent expressions, called 'one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture.'

rows.anchor: EU(Upgrade)=100, EU(DoNothing)=95 ... VOI(Inspection)=20, Cost(Inspection)=5 ... NetVOI=20-5=15>0 ... AcquireInformation is itself the rational action ... gives Zero a mathematical foundation
rows.statement: Worked example: given EU(Upgrade)=100 vs EU(DoNothing)=95, a candidate inspection with VOI=20 and Cost=5 yields NetVOI=15>0, making AcquireInformation itself rational — 'gives Zero a mathematical foundation.'

rows.anchor: Zero_{epistemic} from Zero_{decision} ... a missing fact matters only if resolving it could change something important ... DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap
rows.statement: Refines Zero into Zero_epistemic vs Zero_decision: a knowledge gap matters only if resolving it could change something important — DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap is more important than arbitrary missing information.

lineage_claims.quote: Zero is not merely 'missing data'. This is a major refinement.

rows.anchor: Which Linux kernel version is installed on a test server? ... VOI\approx0 ... Lord should do nothing ... prevents KnowledgeOS from endlessly trying to make itself complete
rows.statement: Worked example: a genuine knowledge gap with VOI≈0 for the current decision means Lord should take no action — prevents pursuing exhaustive completeness.

rows.anchor: should not optimize for CompleteKnowledge. We should optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision ... much more realistic
rows.statement: States the architectural principle: optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision, not CompleteKnowledge — 'both computationally and operationally much more realistic.'

rows.anchor: I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\} ... ReadConfiguration, AskHumanExpert, RunTest, QueryAPI, RunSimulation ... i^*=\arg\max_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] ... a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop
rows.statement: Formalizes information-gathering actions as a candidate set I with per-action Cost and VOI, giving i*=argmax_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] as 'a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop.'

rows.anchor: Restart production server to verify configuration ... Risk(Restart)>0 ... NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) ... Lord cannot blindly maximize information
rows.statement: Worked example showing an information-gathering action (production restart) can itself carry risk, extending net value to NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) — 'Lord cannot blindly maximize information.'

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS=PassiveKnowledgeSystem+ActiveInformationAcquisition when authorized ... a significant conceptual transition
rows.statement: States KnowledgeOS = PassiveKnowledgeSystem + ActiveInformationAcquisition (when authorized) — 'a significant conceptual transition.'

rows.anchor: Exploitation: use current knowledge to act ... Exploration: acquire information ... resembles reinforcement learning and active learning, but KnowledgeOS does not need to become an RL system
rows.statement: Frames Action vs InformationAction as exploitation vs exploration, analogous to reinforcement/active learning, while explicitly not requiring KnowledgeOS to become an RL system.

rows.anchor: VOI(i)>0 does not imply Execute(i) ... VOI(i)>0\Rightarrow Candidate(i) ... Governance\rightarrow Authorization
rows.statement: States a positive VOI only produces a Candidate(i), never automatic Execute(i) — every information-gathering action remains constrained by authorization.

rows.anchor: Aleatoric uncertainty P(Y\mid X) ... Epistemic uncertainty UnknownModel, UnknownParameter, MissingEvidence ... more data may reduce epistemic uncertainty. It generally cannot eliminate genuine aleatoric randomness
rows.statement: Distinguishes aleatoric uncertainty (inherent randomness) from epistemic uncertainty (unknown model/parameter/missing evidence) — more data reduces epistemic but not aleatoric uncertainty.

rows.anchor: Aleatoric uncertainty: 2-5% under the model ... Epistemic uncertainty: firewall configuration not verified ... the second may be reduced through observation
rows.statement: Worked example showing KnowledgeOS should preserve the aleatoric/epistemic distinction in a reported outcome (2-5% aleatoric risk band vs an unverified firewall configuration as epistemic uncertainty reducible via observation).

rows.anchor: Robustness(a) as the stability of the decision across plausible models/parameters ... often more useful than a single expected-value calculation
rows.statement: Defines decision Robustness(a) as stability of the optimal decision across plausible models/parameters, argued as often more useful than a single expected-value calculation.

rows.anchor: a^*=\arg\max_a\min_{M\in\mathcal M}EU_M(a) ... worst-case or robust formulation ... EU(a)=\sum_M P(M\mid E)EU_M(a) ... DecisionRule must be explicit
rows.statement: Contrasts a worst-case/minimax decision rule (argmax_a min_M EU_M(a)) with a model-averaged expected-utility rule, concluding 'DecisionRule must be explicit' since organizations may legitimately choose either.

rows.anchor: DecisionPolicy: scope, admissible actions, constraints, utility/risk model, evidence threshold, escalation rule, authority requirement, revision policy ... prevents business-critical decision logic from disappearing into an AI prompt
rows.statement: Proposes DecisionPolicy as an explicit eight-field DDD domain object, preventing business-critical decision logic from disappearing into an AI prompt.

rows.anchor: Candidate\rightarrow Evaluated\rightarrow Recommended\rightarrow Approved\rightarrow Executed\rightarrow Verified ... Executed\rightarrow Failed or Executed\rightarrow Reversed ... another event-sourced lifecycle
rows.statement: Defines a six-stage event-sourced decision lifecycle (Candidate->Evaluated->Recommended->Approved->Executed->Verified) with Failed/Reversed alternative branches.

rows.anchor: Action\rightarrow Observation ... ExpectedOutcome against ObservedOutcome ... Decision\rightarrow Action\rightarrow Observation\rightarrow ModelEvaluation ... closes the entire system loop
rows.statement: Defines closed-loop decision verification: after execution, compare ExpectedOutcome against ObservedOutcome, feeding Decision->Action->Observation->ModelEvaluation — 'closes the entire system loop.'

rows.anchor: Regret(a,s)=U(a^*(s),s)-U(a,s) ... a useful retrospective metric
rows.statement: Defines decision regret Regret(a,s)=U(a*(s),s)-U(a,s), comparing the taken action to the action that would have been optimal under the true (later-revealed) state — 'a useful retrospective metric.'

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS recommended Upgrade ... later ... DoNothing would have been better ... How costly was the epistemic uncertainty? ... ValueOfKnowledge not just KnowledgeAmount
rows.statement: Worked example showing regret evaluation lets KnowledgeOS assess how costly its epistemic uncertainty was, motivating measuring ValueOfKnowledge rather than mere KnowledgeAmount — 'a profound connection between the epistemic layer and the business layer.'

rows.anchor: E1 cost 1 benefit 2, E2 cost 5 benefit 20, E3 cost 2 benefit 1 ... NetVOI(E_1)=1, NetVOI(E_2)=15, NetVOI(E_3)=-1 ... Lord should prioritize E_2 ... far better than collect all missing information
rows.statement: Worked three-item evidence-prioritization table computing NetVOI for E1/E2/E3, concluding Lord should prioritize E2 — 'far better than collect all missing information.'

rows.anchor: NBA=\arg\max_{x\in X}ExpectedDecisionValue(x) ... Actions+InformationActions+Escalations ... could become one of the core formal definitions of Lord
rows.statement: Defines a mathematical Next-Best-Action formalization NBA=argmax_x ExpectedDecisionValue(x) over Actions+InformationActions+Escalations, proposed as a candidate core formal definition of Lord.

rows.anchor: Lord: What should happen next? under workflow/information/control constraints. Sarathi: Which decision is best supported? given knowledge/models/utility/policy ... exact boundary is a DDD design decision, but the distinction is now mathematically coherent
rows.statement: Restates and sharpens the Lord/Sarathi distinction (Lord: what next; Sarathi: which decision is best supported), explicitly noting the exact boundary is a DDD design choice, not an absolute law, while the underlying distinction is now mathematically coherent.

rows.anchor: Sarathi\rightarrow Recommendation then Human/Board\rightarrow Authorization ... prevents Optimization from being confused with Authority
rows.statement: For high-impact decisions, requires Sarathi to produce only a Recommendation with Human/Board Authorization following separately — preventing Optimization from being confused with Authority.

rows.anchor: Test A probability without utility PASS. Test B high-risk tail RiskPolicy distinguishes PASS. Test C unauthorized optimum NotAdmissible PASS. Test D information value VOI>0 PASS. Test E useless knowledge VOI~=0 NoInformationAction PASS. Test F expensive evidence VOI<Cost DoNotAcquire PASS. Test G ir
rows.statement: Runs eight falsification tests (A-H, all PASS) against the decision-theory model: probability alone cannot determine a decision between differently-consequenced actions; equal-expected-loss actions with different catastrophic tails are distinguished by risk policy; an unauthorized highest-utility action is NotAdmissible; additional evidence with real information value yields VOI>0; an irrelevant knowledge gap yields VOI~=0 and NoInformationAction; evidence costing more than its value yields DoNotAcquire; an irreversible action with large downside can require a HigherEvidenceThreshold if policy specifies it; and executed actions feed back into PredictionEvaluation.

experiment.hypothesis: The expected-utility/VOI/governance decision model behaves correctly across eight representative scenarios.
experiment.setup: Eight scenarios A-H spanning utility-vs-probability, tail risk, authorization constraints, information value (positive, near-zero, and cost-exceeding), irreversibility, and decision feedback.
experiment.assumptions: n/a
experiment.method: apply the EU/VOI/admissibility rules to each scenario
experiment.result: All eight scenarios produce the theoretically expected outcome
experiment.interpretation: Confirms the decision-theoretic model correctly separates probability, utility, risk, authorization, and information value.

rows.anchor: EU, Risk, VOI, Sensitivity, ScenarioAnalysis ... entirely feasible on a normal PC ... a complexity/scaling problem, not a fundamental architecture problem
rows.statement: States the basic decision-theoretic calculations (EU, Risk, VOI, Sensitivity, ScenarioAnalysis) are normal-PC computable; large state spaces, many actions, long horizons, stochastic simulation, and partial observability are scaling, not architectural, problems.

rows.anchor: 25R — PASS ... Decision\neq Inference ... Decision=Optimization under Uncertainty+Utility+Constraints+Authority ... InformationAcquisition is itself a decision ... a rigorous mathematical foundation for Zero\rightarrow Lord\rightarrow Sarathi
rows.statement: Step 25R self-verdict: PASS — Decision ≠ Inference; Decision = Optimization under Uncertainty+Utility+Constraints+Authority; InformationAcquisition is itself a decision — 'a rigorous mathematical foundation for Zero->Lord->Sarathi.'

rows.anchor: World->Observation->Evidence->Assessment->Knowledge->Model->Prediction->Decision->Authorization->Action->Observation ... KnowledgeGap->Zero->Lord->InformationAction->Evidence ... Decision->Outcome->ModelEvaluation->ModelRevision ... a genuine epistemic-control architecture
rows.statement: Presents the full epistemic-decision cycle as a primary loop (World->Observation->Evidence->Assessment->Knowledge->Model->Prediction->Decision->Authorization->Action->Observation) plus two feedback loops (KnowledgeGap->Zero->Lord->InformationAction->Evidence; Decision->Outcome->ModelEvaluation->ModelRevision) — 'a genuine epistemic-control architecture rather than merely an AI knowledge repository.'

rows.anchor: Nexus 3.70 was installed. Which Nexus? Which server? ... Two records can have identical text but refer to different real-world entities ... Identity, Reference, Entity Resolution, Same-As, Distinct-From, Context and Semantic Identity ... Step 25S
rows.statement: Closes by identifying the remaining major boundary — that the whole decision architecture presupposes the system can identify what entity/event/claim is being discussed — and transitions to Step 25S (Identity, Entity Resolution, Same-As, Distinct-From and Knowledge Atma), framing the central question of when KnowledgeOS may legitimately merge two pieces of knowledge as referring to the same thing, and its more dangerous inverse (when it must refuse to merge), explicitly to test whether Knowledge Atma is mathematically/computationally sound enough to serve as the identity foundation for the whole architecture.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 25S — Identity, Entity Resolution, Same-As, Distinct-From and Knowledge Atma

rows.anchor: 10,000,000 assertions ... cannot continuously re-evaluate everything ... How does KnowledgeOS decide what deserves attention? ... NextBestEpistemicAction ... Step 31
rows.statement: Closes by posing the attention-allocation question given a ten-million-assertion knowledge base that cannot be continuously fully re-evaluated, listing six prioritization targets (which knowledge to validate, which conflict to investigate, which model to recalibrate, which evidence to acquire, which decision to revisit, which risk to monitor), transitioning to Step 31 (Epistemic Prioritization, Value of Information, Active Learning, Attention, Resource Allocation, Knowledge Triage) and introducing NextBestEpistemicAction as the target formalization using Value of Information, Expected Loss, Risk, Uncertainty, Dependency Impact, Decision Criticality, and Cost of Investigation.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 31 — Epistemic Prioritization, Value of Information, Active Learning, Attention, Resource Allocation and Knowledge Triage

rows.anchor: Level 1 Claim: Validate(A). Level 2 Investigation: argmax_I NVOI(I). Level 3 Decision: argmin_d E[L(d,Y)]. Level 4 Portfolio: argmax_S Value(S). This hierarchy is extremely important
rows.statement: Formalizes a four-level optimization hierarchy spanning claim validation, investigation selection, decision-making, and portfolio-level allocation.

sources.note: Peer review of the actual executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 numerical results (R5..R2 table), deriving the data-processing-inequality monotonicity theorem for H(Q|R) along a deterministic sequential chain, the sequential-vs-parallel representation family distinction, the H-RR2 Zero-rate-vs-boundary negative result, a revised theory architecture diagram, and a recommendation to audit the corpus/implementation before any Theory v1.3.

rows.anchor: R5 drop timestamps 0.0000 0 YES; R4 round to 3 s.f. 0.4299 35,532 NO; R3 round to 2 s.f. 0.8546 246,235 NO; R2 rank 3.3937 5,530,777 NO
rows.statement: Reports the executed KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 result table across the chain D->R5->R4->R3->R2: R5 (drop timestamps) is empirically adequate (Hhat(Q|R)=0, N_viol=0); R4 (round to 3 s.f.), R3 (round to 2 s.f.), and R2 (rank) are each inadequate with increasing Hhat(Q|R) and N_viol; identifies the first preservation boundary as R5->R4 caused by T4 (rounding to 3 significant digits), but insists the correct scientific statement is scoped to 'for the specified carrier, inquiry Q, contract Pi, transformation chain, and value alphabet V=12, R5 was empirically adequate and R4 was empirically inadequate' rather than a general claim that three significant digits is a universal preservation limit.

rows.anchor: R4 = T4(R5); R3 = T3(R4); R2 = T2(R3) ... data-processing inequality gives H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n) ... adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain.
rows.statement: Derives, via the data-processing inequality applied to the deterministic chain Q->R_n->R_{n-1} (each R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n)), that H(Q|R_5)<=H(Q|R_4)<=H(Q|R_3)<=H(Q|R_2), i.e. adequacy cannot recover later in a deterministic sequential chain; reclassifies the original hypothesis H-C (that adequacy could become non-monotone, e.g. R3 adequate again after R4 inadequate) not as empirically falsified by the data but as structurally ill-posed/a priori inapplicable to this experiment class, recommending the frozen label read '[THEORY/NEG] H-C was ill-posed for the specified sequential deterministic chain; the data-processing inequality makes non-monotone conditional-entropy adequacy impossible' rather than 'H-C refuted a priori', on the ground that a priori impossibility and empirical falsification are epistemically distinct.

rows.anchor: Sequential family: D -> R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 ... No recovery is possible. Parallel family: D -> R_A, D -> R_B, D -> R_C ... Non-monotone comparative behavior is possible here.
rows.statement: Introduces a distinction proposed to become part of the theory: a 'sequential family' of representations (each derived deterministically from the previous one) where H(Q|R) is provably monotone with no recovery possible, versus a 'parallel family' of independently constructed representations from the same source D, where one representation can destroy a distinction while another independently preserves it, so non-monotone comparative adequacy is possible; frames this as the difference between monotonicity along a sequential information-reducing chain and comparative adequacy across independently constructed representations, expected to matter when investigating alternative knowledge representations later.

rows.anchor: Hhat(Q)=5.0098 ... R5=15.042, R4=12.307, R3=11.097, R2=7.170 ... Hhat(R_n) > Hhat(Q) at every level ... empirical consistency with the theoretical bound.
rows.statement: Reports hypothesis H-E's result that empirical Hhat(R_n) exceeds Hhat(Q) at every level of the chain (R5=15.042 through R2=7.170, versus Hhat(Q)=5.0098), matching the expected theoretical lower-bound relationship under the relevant assumptions, and endorses treating this as empirical consistency with the theoretical bound rather than as a proof.

rows.anchor: R5 -> R4 Zero rate 3.77% / R4 -> R3 Zero rate 4.26% / R3 -> R2 Zero rate 0.00% ... does not show a Zero/boundary relationship ... we should not make Zero the fundamental preservation criterion.
rows.statement: Reports hypothesis H-RR2's negative result: measured Zero rates across the chain (3.77%, 4.26%, 0.00%) show no association between Zero and the observed preservation boundary, refuting the original suspicion that Zero -> preservation boundary; concludes Zero should not be treated as the fundamental preservation criterion but as one possible mechanism within a broader architecture that separately includes eliminability/Zero, preservation/adequacy, realization, and reduction cost.

rows.anchor: SOURCE -> Transformation / Representation / Inquiry Q / Preservation contract Pi / Decoder O -> Recoverability/Adequacy -> Preservation boundary -> Eliminability(Zero) / Reduction measures
rows.statement: Proposes a revised overall theory architecture diagram superseding the prior linear trajectory (Vedic transformations -> Zero/eliminability -> relationality -> representation reduction -> preservation): SOURCE branches into Transformation, Representation, Inquiry Q, Preservation contract Pi, and Decoder O, which jointly determine Recoverability/Adequacy, which locates a Preservation boundary, which in turn splits into Eliminability (Zero) and Reduction measures as two downstream, non-foundational consequences.

rows.anchor: A. Mathematical theory: H(Q|R)=0 ... H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) ... R_{n-1}=T_n(R_n) => H(Q|R_{n-1}) >= H(Q|R_n). B. KR-ZERO empirical evidence [list]. C. KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical evidence [list].
rows.statement: Consolidates the current state of knowledge into three tiers: (A) the mathematical theory -- H(Q|R)=0 as the sufficiency/adequacy criterion, the decomposition H(R)=H(Q)+H(R|Q) for adequate deterministic representations, and the monotonicity consequence H(Q|R_{n-1})>=H(Q|R_n); (B) a nine-point list of KR-ZERO empirical findings (Zero is context/transformation/contract-relative, group Zero can differ from member Zero, higher-order determination exists but is not universal, interaction order is not globally monotonic, the phenomenon is transformation-dependent, Zero gives no simple universal kernel/algebra); (C) a ten-point list of KR-REP-REDUCTION empirical findings (observable preservation boundary in a sequential chain, boundary detectable via Q-recoverability, first loss at T4 in this run, reduction is multidimensional, adequacy and realization can diverge, a purely representational recoding can leave recoverability unchanged while altering a fixed decoder, Zero did not correlate with the boundary, contract failure and operator-only failure did not occur, non-monotone adequacy was structurally impossible for this chain).

rows.anchor: At which transformation does the representation cease to preserve the inquiry we care about? ... Given inquiry Q and preservation contract Pi, does representation R still contain enough information to recover Q? ... a potentially powerful foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine.
rows.statement: Frames the practical KnowledgeOS payoff of the representation-reduction results: given a progressive construction chain from raw document through structured representation, claims, relations, normalized claims, knowledge representation, to compressed knowledge representation, the rigorous question 'at which transformation does the representation cease to preserve inquiry Q' can be answered by measuring H(Q|R_n), N_viol(R_n), H(R_n|Q), and representation cost -- proposed as a more rigorous foundation for a KnowledgeOS extraction engine than an informal judgment that summarized information 'still looks present'.

rows.anchor: Sequential reduction: D->R5->R4->R3->R2 ... information sufficiency is monotone. Parallel alternatives: D-> R_A/R_B/R_C ... H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible ... we should preserve it permanently.
rows.statement: Formalizes and endorses permanently preserving the distinction between Sequential Reduction (D->R5->R4->R3->R2, where information sufficiency is monotone by data processing) and Alternative/Parallel Representation Comparison (D branching into R_A, R_B, R_C with no data-processing ordering between them, so H(Q|R_A)<H(Q|R_B) is perfectly possible), naming these two distinct research regimes.

rows.anchor: Representation != Recoverability != Realization, where Representation = what is encoded; Recoverability = what can in principle be reconstructed; Realization = what a particular decoder actually reconstructs.
rows.statement: Formalizes a three-way conceptual distinction -- Representation (what is encoded), Recoverability (what can in principle be reconstructed), and Realization (what a particular decoder actually reconstructs) -- as strictly non-identical properties, proposed to become a major concept in the future KnowledgeOS extraction architecture, sharper than a mere two-way adequacy-vs-realization split.

rows.anchor: R_up =~enc R_down if and only if the implementation demonstrates a bijection between them ... exists f,g: f(R_up)=R_down, g(R_down)=R_up with g o f = id, f o g = id. Only then should we connect this experiment strongly to the existing Q-equivalence research.
rows.statement: Requires that the ascending/descending rank representations only be called equivalent (R_up cong_enc R_down) once the implementation demonstrates an actual bijection f,g between them satisfying g.f=id and f.g=id, and that any residual measured difference in H(Q|R) absent such a bijection be attributed to sampling/estimation or implementation effects rather than treated as evidence of non-equivalence; only a confirmed bijection should connect this result to the existing Q-equivalence research.

rows.statement: Argues that the negative finding Zero != definition of preservation (observed Zero rates 3.77%, 4.26%, 0% showing no demonstrated correspondence with the R5->R4 preservation boundary) is good news because it prevents the KnowledgeOS theory from becoming circular (Zero -> something can be removed -> therefore preservation), providing evidence that Zero, preservation, realization, and reduction are separate research concerns.
