sources.note: KnowledgeOS capability that derives candidate semantic dimensions from a Knower's natural-language intent, context, domain ontology, observation, Zero gaps, Lord horizons and learned patterns, without requiring the Knower to name dimensions explicitly; includes the Semantic Reconstruction sub-capability (structural + semantic-role parsing) and an explicit DimensionAssessment step separating candidate from adopted dimensions. Distinct from the pre-existing dimension-discovery-uncertainty object (B0017), which is about known-vs-unknown-dimension uncertainty rather than this batch's parsing/discovery pipeline.

rows.anchor: Arjuna does not need to know what a dimension is... ObserverIntent \neq DimensionSpecification
rows.statement: Establishes that the Knower's natural-language intent is not itself a dimension specification; KnowledgeOS/Sarathi performs Analyze(Q0,CurrentState,Context) -> CandidateDimensions, so the observer expresses need while the system reconstructs the dimensional schema.

rows.anchor: DimensionDiscovery(Q,K,C) \rightarrow D_{candidate} ... Observation \rightarrow D_{new} ... The two are different.
rows.statement: Introduces Dimension Discovery as a working capability (not yet a domain object) distinct from Observation-driven dimension revelation: DimensionDiscovery(Q,K,C)->D_candidate happens before/independent of Observation->D_new; three sources are named: question-derived (D_Q), observation-derived (D_O), and horizon-derived via Lord (D_L), unioned as D_investigation.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS should generate candidate dimensions, not immediately declare every generated candidate to be a dimension of the observed state.
rows.statement: Corrects the naive Union(D_Q,...,D_Pattern)-as-dimensions model: the union is only a candidate set D^candidate_t; KnowledgeOS must run a separate DimensionAssessment step producing D^adopted, distinguishing CandidateDimension, RelevantDimension, and ObservedDimension as three concepts that must not be collapsed (guards against hallucinated dimensions).

lineage_claims.quote: the union should not yet mean: these are all dimensions of the state

rows.anchor: Pattern -> Candidate, not Pattern -> Fact ... it must still be assessed in the current observation.
rows.statement: Treats pattern-derived candidate dimensions (D_Pattern, e.g. 'dependency relationships are frequently relevant in migrations') as a learning mechanism generating candidates only, never directly as established fact -- another Zero-style safeguard against premature reification.

rows.anchor: When does a candidate dimension become an accepted dimension of the current observation/knowledge state? ... Question 2B — When does a candidate dimension become a dimension of the knowledge state?
rows.statement: Poses Question 2B: the boundary between Dimension Discovery and Knowledge, i.e. under what dimension-status values (UNKNOWN/RELEVANT/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ACCEPTED/REJECTED/NOT_APPLICABLE) a candidate dimension is promoted to an accepted dimension of the knowledge state, deferred ahead of Question 3 (Statement).

rows.anchor: DimensionDiscovery is recursive. The system does not parse the initial question once and finish. It continually reconstructs the semantic space as the investigation develops.
rows.statement: Argues Dimension Discovery must be recursive: a new question Q1 generated from prior discoveries re-enters the language-analysis pipeline (Q1 -> SemanticStructure1 -> D2), linking language analysis to the earlier progressive-investigation levels concretely (Level 0 initial parse, Level 1 relationship discovery, Level 2 duty/obligation, Level 3 consequence dimensions).

rows.anchor: The Sanskrit grammar lens is an analytical lens from which KnowledgeOS may learn useful principles of semantic decomposition. It is not evidence that the KnowledgeOS ontology must conform to Sanskrit grammar... Likewise: The Gita is not proof of our mathematical model.
rows.statement: States an explicit methodological discipline: neither the Sanskrit grammar lens nor the Gita narrative is evidence that KnowledgeOS's ontology must conform to them -- both are sources from which useful structural/semantic principles may be observed and tested, not authoritative specifications.

rows.anchor: \mathcal P : \mathcal L \rightarrow \mathcal S ... \mathcal D : (\mathcal S, \mathcal C, \mathcal K) \rightarrow 2^{\mathcal D_{candidate}} ... D_{candidate} = Union(D_Q, D_C, D_{Domain}, D_{Pattern}, D_{Zero}, D_{Lord})
rows.statement: Gives the batch's most complete formal signatures: a parser P:L->S (with substructural P_struct:L->T and P_sem:L->R), and Dimension Discovery D:(S,C,K)->2^{D_candidate} with the union formula over six named sources, plus a pseudocode algorithm.

rows.anchor: D_{t+1} = \mathcal D(\mathcal P(Q_t), K_t, C_t) ... Discovery terminates when: Z(K_t) = \emptyset or DecisionSufficiency(K_t,I_t) = True
rows.statement: Defines the recursive discovery/investigation/question-generation cycle (Q_t -parse-> S_t -discover-> D_{t+1} -investigate-> K_{t+1} -Zero+Lord-> Q_{t+1}) together with an explicit termination condition: discovery stops when Zero finds no more gaps or decision sufficiency is reached relative to the Ideal state I_t.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS should own the semantic reconstruction capability, while individual parsing technologies remain replaceable implementation mechanisms ... KnowledgeOS \supset Semantic\ Reconstruction \supset Parsing
rows.statement: Decides Semantic Reconstruction is a native KnowledgeOS capability while individual parser technologies (C-type, Sanskrit-type, future LLM-based) are replaceable implementations beneath it: KnowledgeOS superset-of SemanticReconstruction superset-of Parsing.

rows.anchor: The domain capability owns the contract; parsing technologies implement the contract... The architecture should depend on SemanticRepresentation, not CParser or SanskritParser.
rows.statement: Applies a DDD dependency-inversion rule to the parsing question: architecture depends on the SemanticRepresentation contract, never on a specific parser technology; C/Sanskrit parsers become adapters/lenses that implement the contract, not fundamental domain objects.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS should not say: 'Our parser is Sanskrit grammar.' Instead: 'KnowledgeOS requires semantic-role reconstruction; Sanskrit grammar provides one important lens from which we can derive and test the required semantic capabilities.'
rows.statement: Protects the Sanskrit-lens research from over-commitment: it must remain a learning source for deriving/testing semantic capabilities, never an architectural claim that the parser literally is Sanskrit grammar; parser physical placement (in-process/service/library) is explicitly deferred as an infrastructure decision, not an architectural one.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS = SemanticReconstruction + DimensionDiscovery + EpistemicOperations + KnowledgeModel ... Parser \in Implementation of SemanticReconstruction
rows.statement: Formalizes the four-part KnowledgeOS capability sum (SemanticReconstruction + DimensionDiscovery + EpistemicOperations + KnowledgeModel) with a full layered-architecture diagram, and states the final invariant KnowledgeOS != Parser, Parser subset-of KnowledgeOS's Implementation.

rows.anchor: Why Parsing Engines Must Be Replaceable: Reason 1: Technological Evolution... Reason 2: Domain Adaptation... Reason 3: Research and Learning
rows.statement: Gives three reasons parser implementations must remain replaceable: technology evolves (C/Sanskrit-style parsers today, LLM/neural parsers tomorrow), different domains need different specialized parsers (software vs legal vs medical), and the project must be able to learn from multiple grammatical/linguistic traditions without permanent dependency on any one.

rows.anchor: KnowledgeOS \leftarrow LearnFrom(Sanskrit Grammar) ... KnowledgeOS \neq Implement(Sanskrit Grammar)
rows.statement: States the 'Learning Principle': KnowledgeOS learns architectural insight from Sanskrit grammar without implementing/adopting it as the domain ontology.

rows.anchor: Intent \rightarrow Structural\ Analysis \rightarrow Semantic\ Reconstruction \rightarrow Context\ Interpretation \rightarrow Domain\ Model \rightarrow Candidate\ Dimensions \rightarrow Observation \rightarrow Dimension\ Discovery
rows.statement: Corrects 'Question -> DimensionDiscovery' to a longer pipeline: Intent -> Structural Analysis -> Semantic Reconstruction -> Context Interpretation -> Domain Model -> Candidate Dimensions -> Observation -> Dimension Discovery, establishing Parsing ≠ DimensionDiscovery (parsing is an input capability to it). Also renames the earlier C-type/Sanskrit-grammar parser pair as Structural Language Analysis (Parser_S(Q)->SyntaxStructure) and Semantic Reconstruction (Parser_M(Q,C)->SemanticStructure), with DimensionDiscovery = f(Syntax, Semantics, Context, Domain, Knowledge); clarifies the 'Sanskrit lens' is not literal Sanskrit-grammar implementation but the requirement that natural language be reconstructed into semantic roles/relations, not merely syntactically parsed.

rows.anchor: The kernel does not merely ask: How much knowledge do I have? It first determines: Along which dimensions should this knowledge be understood? ... D_t = {d_1,...,d_{n_t}} ... n_t != n_{t+1}. ... knowledge growth is not only movement within a fixed space; it can involve discovering new dimensions of the space.
rows.statement: At each time t the kernel first determines along which dimensions knowledge should be understood, not merely how much it has: D_t={d_1,...,d_{n_t}}, with the number of dimensions itself able to change (n_t != n_{t+1}). Knowledge purification can therefore be D_t->D_{t+1} as well as K_t->K_{t+1}: knowledge growth is not only movement within a fixed space but can involve discovering new dimensions of the space.

rows.anchor: A dimension should not merely be a field. D_i = an independently discriminable aspect of the knowledge state. For example D_t={Version,Availability,Security,Backup,Network,Ownership}. K_t={Version=3.69,Availability=99.2%,Security=?,Backup=Valid,Network=Unknown,Ownership=TeamA}. '?' does not necessarily mean the dimension doesn't exist. It means D_i in D_t and v_i(t)=Unknown. That is different from D_i notin D_t.
rows.statement: Defines a dimension formally as 'an independently discriminable aspect of the knowledge state,' illustrated with a six-dimension worked example (Version, Availability, Security, Backup, Network, Ownership) with mixed known/unknown values, establishing that an unknown-valued '?' entry means D_i in D_t and v_i(t)=Unknown -- categorically different from the dimension simply not being in D_t.

aliases: reasoning that tests vs reasoning that produces knowledge

sources.note: The recurring claim that tarka (hypothetical/reductio reasoning that tests claims) must be architecturally separated from anumana (inference that produces knowledge); reinforced across S0219, S0220, S0222, S0223, S0224 as one of the batch's strongest candidates.

rows.anchor: Tarka is a kind of conjectural reasoning (uha)... Tarka is NOT an independent pramana... It is 'Pramana-anugrahaka' — an assistant to the pramanas.
rows.statement: Cites Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy definitions of tarka as conjectural reasoning that reveals a thing's real nature by showing the absurdity of contrary characters, and as explicitly not an independent pramana but an assistant to the pramanas (does not itself produce definitive cognition; functions as reductio ad absurdum / prasanga).

rows.anchor: Five Types of Tarka (Fallacious Structures to Avoid): Pramanabadhita, Atmasraya, Anyonyasraya, Cakrakasraya, Anavastha
rows.statement: Lists tarka's function as reductio ad absurdum with a worked example (self as eternal vs produced, via karmic-inheritance absurdity), and enumerates five fallacious-tarka structures to avoid: contradicted-by-valid-knowledge, self-dependency, mutual dependency, circular dependency, infinite regress.

rows.anchor: Status: Apramana (not a knowledge source) vs Pramana (valid knowledge source) ... Function: Tests competing claims, removes doubt vs Derives new knowledge from evidence
rows.statement: Full comparison table of Tarka vs Anumana across status (apramana/pramana), function (tests vs derives), independence (assistant vs independent source), outcome (eliminates alternatives/confirms vyapti vs produces valid inference), and worked examples.

rows.anchor: reason (tarka) must serve scripture (sruti), not replace it ... Dustarkat suviramyatam — Srutimatas tarko'nusandhiyatam ... Should KnowledgeOS reasoning be constrained by organizational authority? The Vedic model suggests: Yes
rows.statement: Cites Sankaracarya's warning against dustarka (corrupt/futile reasoning contrary to authority) and Nyaya's self-conception as a rational defender of Hindu religious culture, then argues this raises the architectural question of whether KnowledgeOS reasoning should be constrained by organizational authority, answering 'Yes' by analogy, aligning with Evidence != Authority / Assessment != Authority.

rows.anchor: Candidate TARKA-003: Tarka as Assistant — Reasoning that tests claims (tarka) is distinct from reasoning that produces knowledge (anumana). Strong candidate — reinforces existing distinctions.
rows.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-003: reasoning that tests claims (tarka) is distinct from reasoning that produces knowledge (anumana); classified 'strong candidate'.

rows.anchor: Candidate TARKA-005: Authority Constraint on Reason — Reasoning must respect organizational authority boundaries (no 'dustarka' — futile reasoning contrary to authority). Strong candidate.
rows.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-005: reasoning must respect organizational authority boundaries (no dustarka); classified 'strong candidate', said to reinforce existing governance principles.

rows.anchor: Tarka as kernel primitive | Rejected | None ... Nyaya as complete architecture | Rejected | Dangerous
rows.statement: Final classification table explicitly rejects treating Tarka as a kernel primitive (kernel relevance: none) and treating Nyaya as a complete architecture (kernel relevance: 'Dangerous'), while classifying tarka-as-assistant and authority-constraint-on-reason as 'Strong candidate' with High kernel relevance.

rows.anchor: Tarka Shastra could simplify KnowledgeOS by... However, it could complicate KnowledgeOS by... Answer: Context-dependent... Recommended Approach: Treat Tarka Shastra concepts as a research lens for reasoning and epistemology components, not as a requirement for the entire KnowledgeOS architecture.
rows.statement: Final strategic assessment weighs simplification (structured epistemological foundations, formal reasoning methodology, reinforced Authority!=Evidence, contradiction detection) against complication (epistemological overhead, mandatory pramana grounding, non-generalizing Vedic authority constraints), concluding 'context-dependent' and recommending treatment as a research lens, not an architecture requirement, with three strongest candidates named (tarka-as-assistant, authority-constraint-on-reason, structured-doubt).

rows.anchor: EXTERNAL RESEARCH != KNOWLEDGEOS ARCHITECTURE... Do not design the kernel. Do not choose technology. Do not define bounded contexts. Do not create ADRs. Do not propose migration. The output is an independent research evidence base for a later architecture decision.
rows.statement: Final discipline statement: distinguishes what external research establishes (what is known in the field) from what EKS/PKS/AIP archaeology establishes (what KnowledgeOS actually has); only their comparison can determine relevance; the document explicitly bars itself from designing the kernel, choosing technology, defining bounded contexts, creating ADRs, or proposing migration, self-classifying as 'NOT ARCHITECTURE EVIDENCE / NO KERNEL DECISION'.

rows.anchor: H-KOS-Reasoning-Separation-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL distinguish reasoning that produces knowledge from reasoning that evaluates, challenges, or eliminates knowledge... Inference creates candidates. Tarka tests candidates.
rows.statement: Proposes candidate invariant H-KOS-Reasoning-Separation-001, described as 'probably the strongest candidate': separate an Inference Engine (creates knowledge candidates) from a Critical Reasoning Engine (tests/challenges/eliminates candidates).

rows.anchor: Knower -> Observation -> Evidence Layer -> Reasoning Layer (Inference/Analogy/Deduction/Abduction) -> Validation Layer (Tarka/Contradiction Check/Fallacy Detection) -> Knowledge State -> Decision Support
rows.statement: Presents an updated cognitive-architecture diagram combining all research lenses so far (Vani, Zero, Gita, Vedanta, Tripuṭī, Epistemic Control Systems, TMS/AGM, Tarka Shastra), separating a Reasoning Layer (knowledge-producing) from a Validation Layer (knowledge-testing).

rows.anchor: What Tarka Does NOT Add: New kernel dimension, New bounded context, New storage model, New authority model, AI architecture decision.
rows.statement: Explicitly disciplines the extraction: Tarka does not add a new kernel dimension, bounded context, storage model, authority model, or AI architecture decision, warning against 'turning Tarka into a complete architecture or kernel primitive'.

rows.anchor: Many AI systems collapse: Observed and Inferred. KnowledgeOS cannot... INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the distinction between directly observed knowledge and knowledge derived through reasoning.
rows.statement: Uses the smoke/fire anumana example to argue inference is a transformation, not a source, and proposes INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001 to keep Observation and Inference structurally distinct.

rows.anchor: Tarka Is Not Truth Generation — It Is Truth Filtering... KnowledgeOS should have: Reasoning Gate. Not: Answer Generator. INV-KOS-ReasoningGate-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL separate hypothesis generation from epistemic validation.
rows.statement: Diagrams a Candidate Claim -> Tarka -> {invalid reasoning | insufficient evidence | contradiction} -> Accepted reasoning path pipeline and proposes INV-KOS-ReasoningGate-001.

rows.anchor: a supportive argument stage (tarka) used when doubts arise about the implication between evidence and conclusion... Not: Generate truth. but: Test whether reasoning survives examination.
rows.statement: Restates tarka's role as a reasoning validator invoked specifically when doubt arises about an evidence-to-conclusion implication, not as a truth-generation mechanism.

rows.anchor: tarka as 'suppositional reasoning': reasoning used to expose problems in an opponent's view, but not itself a knowledge source... Agent B disagrees => Agent B is right (bad) ... AI Debate Agent -> Tarka Engine -> Verification Engine
rows.statement: Frames tarka as an 'Architectural Challenge Engine' for AI debate agents, explicitly warning against the bad pattern of treating disagreement itself as proof of correctness, requiring instead that a challenge stress-test reasoning and then require a valid knowledge source.

rows.anchor: Lakṣaṇa — definition adequacy ... Vyāpti — the hidden invariant test ... Hetvābhāsa — attack the reason itself ... Saṃśaya — don't collapse unresolved alternatives ... Abhāva — absence needs a counter-correlate ... Nigrahasthāna — identify where an argument has actually failed
rows.statement: Derives a nine-family falsification instrument from the Tarka-sangraha (with Dipika commentary), explicitly as an instrument rather than a source of content: (1) Laksana definition adequacy, (2) Paksa-Sadhya-Hetu discipline (claim/thing-to-prove/reason kept distinct), (3) Vyapti hidden-invariant test (is the claimed universal relation actually universal), (4) Hetvabhasa (fallacy classes in the reason), (5) Samsaya (do not collapse unresolved alternatives prematurely), (6) Viparyaya (erroneous apprehension/misattribution), (7) Abhava (unqualified negative claims need a counter-correlate), (8) Anvaya-Vyatireka (one-sided causal inference), (9) Nigrahasthana (identify where an argument has actually failed); operationalizes family 1 directly as 'does our definition of the Kernel have avyapti (under-inclusion), ativyapti (over-inclusion), or asambhava (impossibility under the Constitution)?'.

lexical.anchor: Tarka is a kind of conjectural reasoning (uha)... Tarka is NOT an independent pramana... It is 'Pramana-anugrahaka' — an assistant to the pramanas.

conceptual.anchor: Five Types of Tarka (Fallacious Structures to Avoid): Pramanabadhita, Atmasraya, Anyonyasraya, Cakrakasraya, Anavastha

formal.anchor: Knower -> Observation -> Evidence Layer -> Reasoning Layer (Inference/Analogy/Deduction/Abduction) -> Validation Layer (Tarka/Contradiction Check/Fallacy Detection) -> Knowledge State -> Decision Support

governance.anchor: Tarka Shastra could simplify KnowledgeOS by... However, it could complicate KnowledgeOS by... Answer: Context-dependent... Recommended Approach: Treat Tarka Shastra concepts as a research lens for reasoning and epistemology components, not as a requirement for the entire KnowledgeOS architecture.

rationale_evidence.anchor: reason (tarka) must serve scripture (sruti), not replace it ... Dustarkat suviramyatam — Srutimatas tarko'nusandhiyatam ... Should KnowledgeOS reasoning be constrained by organizational authority? The Vedic model suggests: Yes
rationale_evidence.statement: Cites Sankaracarya's warning against dustarka (corrupt/futile reasoning contrary to authority) and Nyaya's self-conception as a rational defender of Hindu religious culture, then argues this raises the architectural question of whether KnowledgeOS reasoning should be constrained by organizational authority, answering 'Yes' by analogy, aligning with Evidence != Authority / Assessment != Authority.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Tarka Shastra could simplify KnowledgeOS by... However, it could complicate KnowledgeOS by... Answer: Context-dependent... Recommended Approach: Treat Tarka Shastra concepts as a research lens for reasoning and epistemology components, not as a requirement for the entire KnowledgeOS architecture.
rationale_evidence.statement: Final strategic assessment weighs simplification (structured epistemological foundations, formal reasoning methodology, reinforced Authority!=Evidence, contradiction detection) against complication (epistemological overhead, mandatory pramana grounding, non-generalizing Vedic authority constraints), concluding 'context-dependent' and recommending treatment as a research lens, not an architecture requirement, with three strongest candidates named (tarka-as-assistant, authority-constraint-on-reason, structured-doubt).

sources.note: Fifth governing verification directive (post-Step-240), directly operationalizing THEORY-GAP-MAP-001's minimum-path findings into 10 explicit numbered tasks: build a ~25-concept foundational dependency graph, reconstruct K from first principles across all candidates with a strict verdict vocabulary, solve the epistemic-status crosswalk problem, formally define equality/identity on K (with a mandatory not-conflated list), break all circular definitions with genuine-vs-legitimate-recursion classification, computationally instantiate the smallest concrete knowledge state and execute 10 operations on it, formally test the transition function's totality/determinism/composability, and test whether knowledge must be separated from governance into a typed family rather than one universal kernel -- plus a historical concept trace, a real-empirical-test requirement, a mathematics-quality gate, an explicit measure-theory audit, a 5-domain (mathematical/statistical/DDD/engineering/empirical) final decision gate, 13 named required outputs, and a governing rule that the verifier must not solve the theory FOR the authors, only determine whether the corpus already contains enough information to solve itself.

rows.anchor: The objective is NOT to make the theory work. The objective is to determine, with evidence, whether it CAN be made to work without silently repairing, inventing, or retrospectively rewriting the corpus.
rows.statement: The foundational reconstruction audit reframes the entire verification objective: not to make KnowledgeOS theory work, but to determine with evidence whether it CAN be made to work without silently repairing, inventing, or retrospectively rewriting the corpus.

rows.anchor: 1. The corpus contains multiple kernel candidates and at least two competing kernel lineages. ... 10. The feedback loop between the corpus and the verification programme must now be explicitly controlled. 11. The corpus's historical evolution must not be treated as proof that its latest formulation
rows.statement: An 11-item baseline of findings is frozen as the verified starting point (not to be weakened by later steps' stronger claims): multiple competing kernel lineages, K not unambiguously defined, downstream operators unevaluable, all three completenesses NO, competing epistemic-status vocabularies, undefined equality/identity on K, circular definitions involving K/T/validation, at least one independently confirmed mathematical error, much purported empirical validation being specification rather than execution, the corpus-verifier feedback loop requiring explicit control, and historical evolution not being proof of latest-formulation correctness.

rows.anchor: Stop asking: What does the next step say? Instead ask: What is the minimum formal core that must exist for KnowledgeOS theory to be a valid theory at all? ... Do not assume beforehand that the answer is K = {(q,s,e,c,t,u)}. That is currently a verifier recommendation, NOT a corpus-established result
rows.statement: The central question is explicitly changed from 'what does the next step say' to 'what is the minimum formal core that must exist for KnowledgeOS theory to be a valid theory at all', derived from the corpus and mathematical/engineering necessity -- and explicitly warns not to assume the verifier's own prior recommended K={(q,s,e,c,t,u)} is correct without testing it, since it remains a recommendation, not a corpus-established result.

rows.anchor: Object | Definition exists? | Type exists? | Depends on | Used by | Circular? | Computable? | Empirically tested? ... 25 objects
rows.statement: Task 1 mandates a formal foundational dependency graph over ~25 named theory objects (K, knowledge item/proposition, epistemic status, evidence, provenance/lineage, context, temporal validity, uncertainty, identity/equality, transformation, policy, authority, validation, governance, observation, assessment, action, history/replay, invariants, requirements, satisfaction relation, composition, supersession, contradiction, missingness, unknown) via a 7-column table, requiring a mathematically usable definition test, not mere occurrence counting.

rows.anchor: Do NOT select the newest candidate merely because it is newer. Do NOT select the candidate with the most components merely because it represents more concepts. ... ESTABLISHED / SUPPORTED / PARTIALLY SUPPORTED / UNDER-SPECIFIED / CONTRADICTED / REFUTED / VERIFIER PROPOSAL.
rows.statement: Task 2 mandates reconstructing K from first principles across every serious candidate (10-point per-candidate checklist: source, semantics, type, constructors, equality, membership, admissible/invalid states, instantiability, component-definedness), compared on 15 mathematical criteria, explicitly forbidding selecting the newest or most-component-rich candidate by default, using a 7-value closed verdict vocabulary, output to K-CANDIDATE-COMPARISON.md.

rows.anchor: A. equivalent, B. conservative extensions, C. refinements, D. genuinely competing ontologies, E. merely different linguistic labels. ... If no canonical vocabulary can be derived from the corpus, state: CANONICAL STATUS VOCABULARY NOT DERIVABLE FROM CORPUS. Do not invent one and call it verified.
rows.statement: Task 3 mandates a complete epistemic-status-vocabulary crosswalk before any canonical vocabulary may be proposed, classifying the relationship between competing vocabularies into 5 categories (equivalent, conservative extension, refinement, genuinely competing ontology, merely different label), with an explicit fallback statement 'CANONICAL STATUS VOCABULARY NOT DERIVABLE FROM CORPUS' if none can be derived -- forbidding inventing one and calling it verified.

rows.anchor: K1=K2 ... x\in K ... two knowledge items to be identical ... two states to have the same semantic content. These concepts MUST NOT be conflated. ... structural equality, semantic equality, observational equivalence, identity, version identity. ... This section must contain actual formal definitions,
rows.statement: Task 4 mandates formally defining (or proving impossible to define) 5 distinct equality/identity notions (structural, semantic, observational equivalence, identity, version identity) that must never be conflated, then determining which equality is actually required by each of Replay/Merge/Supersede/Diff/Transition/Provenance/Validation -- requiring actual formal definitions, not prose.

rows.anchor: K\rightarrow T\rightarrow K ... K\rightarrow validation\rightarrow K ... K\rightarrow status(E,K)\rightarrow K ... determine whether it is genuine circularity or legitimate recursive definition; ... whether a base case exists; ... Do not repair the definition silently. ... VERIFIER PROPOSED REPAIR.
rows.statement: Task 5 mandates a dedicated dependency-cycle audit specifically testing the exact circular constructions already found (K->T->K, K->validation->K, K->status(E,K)->K), for each determining genuine-circularity-vs-legitimate-recursion, base-case existence, termination, and fixed-point-interpretation intent -- any possible repair recorded separately and explicitly as VERIFIER PROPOSED REPAIR, never silently applied.

rows.anchor: construct the smallest possible concrete knowledge state. Use a toy example. ... Then compute: 1. membership; ... 10. state transition. If any operation cannot be computed from the definitions, STOP and record the missing definition. Do not write pseudo-code and call it execution.
rows.statement: Task 6 mandates constructing and actually instantiating the smallest possible concrete toy knowledge state (one proposition, evidence item, context, epistemic status, temporal validity interval, uncertainty representation, provenance relation) and computing 10 operations on it (membership, equality, contradiction, supersession, addition, removal, transformation, validation, provenance lookup, state transition), stopping and recording the exact missing definition wherever an operation cannot be computed -- pseudo-code does not count as execution.

rows.anchor: Is it total? Is it partial? Is it deterministic? ... What happens when evidence is missing? ... when policy rejects the transformation? ... Construct at least one concrete transition. Execute it. Record input state, transformation, output state and all derived values.
rows.statement: Task 7 mandates formally testing the transition function T's totality, determinism, computability, composability, identity-preservation, and typing-preservation, plus behavior under 4 named failure conditions (missing evidence, conflicting evidence, absent authority, policy rejection, validation failure), requiring at least one concrete transition to be constructed and actually executed with full input/output/derived-value recording.

rows.anchor: Determine whether the theory requires a typed family such as: KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History rather than one universal kernel. ... Is this a state, a relation, an operation, an assessment, a constraint, an actor-dependent authorization, or a historical propert
rows.statement: Task 8 mandates formally testing whether knowledge must be separated from governance into a typed family of 6 distinct object kinds (KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History) rather than forced into one universal kernel -- a DDD question as much as a mathematical one, asking of every object whether it is a state, relation, operation, assessment, constraint, actor-dependent authorization, or historical property, forbidding forcing all nouns into entities or all concepts into state.

rows.anchor: origin -> refinement -> contradiction -> resolution -> current definition. ... RETAINED, REFINED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, HISTORICAL ONLY, VERIFIER PROPOSAL. ... the proper way to preserve the evolutionary nature of the corpus without assuming newer = correct.
rows.statement: Task 10 mandates tracing surviving foundational concepts back through the 001-240 evolution only AFTER the foundational analysis is complete, classifying each into a 7-value vocabulary (RETAINED, REFINED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, HISTORICAL ONLY, VERIFIER PROPOSAL), not requiring every historical statement to survive -- the proper way to preserve the corpus's evolutionary nature without assuming newer=correct.

rows.anchor: Do not accept PASS/verified/falsification test/simulation/evidence-based unless an actual empirical act exists. ... If the repository contains an implementation relevant to KnowledgeOS, inspect it. If no implementation exists, say: NO IMPLEMENTATION AVAILABLE FOR EMPIRICAL VALIDATION.
rows.statement: Empirical validation is mandated to become genuinely real: no textual PASS/verified/simulation label is accepted without an actual empirical act (exact input, command/program, output, expected vs observed result, interpretation, evidence class); the actual repository must be inspected if an implementation exists, with the explicit fallback 'NO IMPLEMENTATION AVAILABLE FOR EMPIRICAL VALIDATION' rather than manufacturing one.

rows.anchor: Do NOT conclude merely from the directory name that measure theory is part of the final theory. ... sigma-algebra, measurable space, measure, probability measure, random variable, ... If measure theory is unnecessary for the final core, state so explicitly.
rows.statement: An explicit measure-theory audit is mandated against the corpus's own folder name 'phase_measure_theory': 12 named formal measure-theoretic concepts (sigma-algebra, measurable space, measure, probability measure, random variable, conditional probability, expectation, filtration, stochastic process, Lebesgue integration, Radon-Nikodym, Dempster-Shafer remnants) must each be checked for whether they are genuinely required/actually used/formally defined/abandoned/merely historical -- explicitly forbidding concluding measure theory is part of the final theory merely from the directory name.

rows.anchor: Mathematical ... Statistical ... DDD ... Engineering ... Empirical ... Do NOT attempt to declare the KnowledgeOS theory complete until all of the following are answered.
rows.statement: The final decision gate requires explicit answers across 5 domains (Mathematical: 13 questions about K/equality/membership/uncertainty/provenance/transformation/computability/composition/proof; Statistical: 7 questions about randomness/uncertainty/distributions/observation/evidence/assumptions/testing; DDD: 7 questions about canonical concepts/types/grouping/relations/operations/governance/UL stability; Engineering: 8 questions about instantiability/serialization/computable-equality/executable-transformation/validation/provenance/replay/failure-representation; Empirical: 5 questions about what was executed/inspected/failed/survived/untested) before the theory may be declared complete.

rows.anchor: Do NOT solve the theory for the authors. Your job is to determine whether the theory already contains enough information to solve itself. If the corpus does not determine a unique answer, report: UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS.
rows.statement: The most important rule: the verifier must not solve the theory FOR the authors, only determine whether the theory already contains enough information to solve itself -- reporting UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS where no unique answer exists, listing all valid reconstructions where several exist, and explicitly listing any new assumptions or genuinely missing mathematics required.

rows.anchor: Stop and report to supervision if you reach a point where: two candidate definitions remain equally defensible; ... a repair would materially change the theory rather than merely clarify notation. ... the exact boundary between WHAT THE KNOWLEDGEOS CORPUS ESTABLISHES and WHAT A FUTURE THEORY WOULD H
rows.statement: The stop condition triggers supervision whenever two candidate definitions remain equally defensible, a choice requires a normative/domain decision, a definition cannot be derived from the corpus, empirical validation needs an unavailable system, or a repair would materially change (not merely clarify) the theory -- the purpose of the entire phase is establishing the exact boundary between what the KnowledgeOS corpus establishes and what a future theory would have to add, only after which the project can decide to reconstruct, amend, split, or reject parts of the theory.

rows.anchor: We must not force every operation into T:K->K because Step 255 already demonstrated that some operations may depend on external policy, authority, time, evidence or other typed context.
rows.statement: Applies Step 255's finding directly: no operation should be forced into the shape T:K->K, since operations may legitimately depend on external typed context (policy, authority, time, evidence) rather than K alone.

rows.anchor: Add requires a definition of identity/equality. This directly links Step 256 back to the unresolved Equality_K. ... set-like semantics Add(K,x)=K union {x} [versus] identity-aware semantics [which] may reject an object whose identity already exists.
rows.statement: Shows Add cannot be formally defined until equality/identity is resolved, since two radically different semantics remain open: plain set-union (duplicates silently absorbed) versus identity-aware rejection of objects whose identity already exists.

rows.anchor: Does removal mean x not-in K' or x in K' with status Withdrawn? These are radically different semantics. ... Remove != Withdraw unless the vocabulary explicitly decides otherwise. ... Reject(x) != Remove(x). This is an important Ubiquitous Language distinction.
rows.statement: Distinguishes true deletion from lifecycle-status change as radically different operation semantics, concluding Remove != Withdraw and Reject != Remove unless the theory explicitly decides to identify them -- since a status-changed object remains represented in K while a deleted one does not.

rows.anchor: revision requires identity preservation: id(x')=id(x)? If yes, Revision(x,x') is a state transition on one entity. If no, Revision is actually Remove(x)+Add(x'). ... What makes two knowledge objects 'the same object' across revision? ... This is another reason why equality and identity cannot be pos
rows.statement: Shows Revise cannot be formally defined until cross-time object identity is resolved: if id(x')=id(x), Revise is a genuine state transition on one entity; if not, Revise reduces to Remove+Add of two different entities -- the same identity/equality dependency recurring across multiple operations.

rows.anchor: Provenance(x3) = {Provenance(x1), Provenance(x2)}. If so, Merge is inherently provenance-preserving. This means that the operation registry itself can reveal whether provenance is operationally essential. ... Split requires a preservation invariant.
rows.statement: Shows Merge is diagnostically important for the provenance question: if the merged object's provenance is the union of its sources' provenances, Merge is inherently provenance-preserving, meaning the operation registry itself (not abstract argument) can reveal whether provenance is operationally essential; separately notes Split requires an explicit semantic-preservation invariant across its decomposition.

rows.anchor: Every semantically relevant external variable must be explicit. ... T: K x Policy x Time -> K'. This is preferable to hiding Policy or Time inside an implicit global context. ... Deterministic Transformation != Immutable Knowledge.
rows.statement: States a determinism-discipline principle: any externally-varying quantity a transformation depends on (e.g. current time, applicable policy) must be an explicit function argument, never an implicit global, or the transformation appears nondeterministic to the mathematical model; separately clarifies determinism (same inputs, same result) is orthogonal to immutability of the overall knowledge base.

rows.anchor: R(T_i) = (Name, Domain, Codomain, Preconditions, Postconditions, Invariants, Parameters, Dependencies, Determinism, ProvenanceDependency, HistoryDependency, PolicyDependency, IdentityDependency) becomes the working registry schema.
rows.statement: Defines the working operation-registry schema R(T_i) with 13 fields, extending the mandate's original 9-field proposal with explicit PolicyDependency and IdentityDependency flags.

rows.anchor: we should not assume closure: T_i,T_j in T => T_j o T_i in T. The earlier audit already found that the governed transformation subset is not demonstrated closed under composition.
rows.statement: Reaffirms the corpus's established finding that the governed transformation subset is not closed under composition, applying it to the operation-registry construction: composition T_j o T_i is only meaningful when Codomain(T_i) intersects Domain(T_j), and closure must never be assumed.

rows.anchor: T_Add: K x X -> K, T_Merge: K x X x X -> K, Validate: K x E -> Result, Approve: Candidate x Authority -> ApprovedCandidate. Therefore KnowledgeOS may be better modeled as a typed transition system than as a single algebra.
rows.statement: Confirms operations need not share one homogeneous signature shape by giving 4 explicitly differently-typed example operations, reaffirming the typed-transition-system (not single algebra) conclusion already reached in Steps 249-250.

rows.anchor: Validate not-equiv Transform. This prevents a common category error in the kernel. ... Command is not Transformation ... Command -> Decision -> Transformation -> NewState ... Event != T. The corpus already distinguishes Command -> Transformation -> Event.
rows.statement: Reaffirms three category-error-preventing non-collapses for the operation vocabulary: Validate != Transform (validation may determine valid/invalid without changing K); Command != Transformation (command is intent/request, not the state change itself); Event != Transformation (an event records an occurrence, distinct from the state-evolution-defining function).

rows.anchor: ProvDep(T_i) in {0,1,?} ... This gives us a way to empirically determine where history must survive. ... transforms the vague question 'Does provenance belong in K?' into the operational question: exists T in T: ProvDep(T)=1? If yes, then provenance-sensitive information must be available to that op
rows.statement: Converts the recurring vague 'does provenance belong in K' question into a precise operational test using explicit per-operation dependency flags (ProvDep, HistDep, PolicyDep in {0,1,?}): if any operation has ProvDep=1, provenance-sensitive information must be accessible to it, and only then does the placement question (K-resident, T-parameter, or external context) arise -- directly implementing S1621's Type-I/II/III taxonomy as a concrete research tool.

rows.anchor: Required(T) = StateReq(T) union ContextReq(T). Only StateReq(T) constrains K. ... K* = argmin_K Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency.
rows.statement: Refines the kernel-minimization target by splitting an operation's total required information into StateReq(T) (must be resident in K) and ContextReq(T) (may be supplied externally, does not constrain K), restating the optimization target K*=argmin Complexity(K) subject to semantic sufficiency with this refined split.

rows.anchor: T must be typed before K can be minimized. Operations may be partial. Operations need not share one homogeneous signature. Validation, Command, Event and Transformation must not be conflated. Provenance/History/Policy dependence must be explicitly tested per operation. Not established: the nine cand
rows.statement: Consolidates the step's established-versus-not-established results: established that T must be typed before K can be minimized, operations may be partial, need not share one signature, and 4 key terms must not be conflated, with dependency-testing mandatory per operation; explicitly not established that the 9 candidate operations or any particular signature is final.

rows.anchor: The most important unresolved signatures are: Supersede, Merge, Revise, Transform. These operations have the highest potential to distinguish competing state/history models. ... rows.statement: Names Supersede, Merge, Revise and Transform as the 4 highest-value operations for distinguishing competing state/history models, and sets Step 257 as their complete formalization (across domain/codomain/preconditions/postconditions/identity/provenance/history/policy/determinism/composability) in order to run the first real congruence experiment -- explicitly judged stronger evidence than proposing yet another candidate kernel tuple.

sources.note: An executed placement matrix determining, test by test, which provenance/lineage/history-related questions are answerable from K=(A,R) alone: assertion provenance and lineage (via R_der reachability) are answerable; transition provenance, merge provenance, withdrawal record, contestation record, evidence provenance, and source-independence are all NOT answerable from K alone.

rows.anchor: lineage from K alone : [] -- empty, correctly: no ancestors ... history from K alone : NOT ANSWERABLE ... => Step 265 s265.2's base-case argument CONFIRMED by construction: at t=0 lineage is empty, so any model that DEFINES provenance as 'lineage of the history' has nothing to define it with. Provenance must be carried, not derived. This is the strongest single argument in Step 265.
rows.statement: TEST 1 confirms by construction Step 265 s265.2's base-case argument: for an assertion imported at t=0, provenance is answerable directly from K (carried in Pi), lineage computed from K is correctly empty (no ancestors), but history is not answerable from K alone -- K cannot distinguish 'imported at t=0' from 'asserted at t=0 by a person'; concludes provenance must be carried rather than derived from history, since at t=0 there is no history to derive it from.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 265 s265.2's base-case argument CONFIRMED by construction

experiment.hypothesis: provenance can be derived from lineage/history rather than carried directly on the assertion.
experiment.setup: a single assertion a0 imported at t=0 with no ancestors
experiment.assumptions: lineage is computed as reachability via derives/refers edges
experiment.method: query provenance, lineage, and history from K0 alone
experiment.result: provenance answerable via Pi; lineage empty (correctly, no ancestors); history not answerable at all
experiment.interpretation: since at t=0 lineage is empty, a provenance definition based on lineage-of-history has nothing to operate on
experiment.conclusion: CONFIRMED: provenance must be carried, not derived

rows.anchor: who performed the restatus, and when? NOT ANSWERABLE FROM K ... Pi records the origin of the CLAIM, not the origin of the STATE CHANGE. The theory has provenance for assertions and NO provenance for transitions. Step 265's placement matrix has no row for transition provenance.
rows.statement: TEST 2 shows that after a one-step transformation (restatus), provenance Pi is unchanged/preserved on the assertion, but who performed the restatus and when is not answerable from K, demonstrating Pi records the origin of a claim, not the origin of a state change, and Step 265's placement matrix has no row for transition provenance at all.

experiment.hypothesis: provenance as currently placed (on the assertion) also records who/when performed a state transition.
experiment.setup: apply a restatus operation to an existing assertion and inspect Pi before/after
experiment.assumptions: Pi is carried unchanged through operations that don't explicitly modify it
experiment.inputs: K0 with a0, then T(K0, restatus(a0,Accepted))
experiment.method: compare Pi before and after; check for any record of who/when performed the restatus
experiment.result: Pi unchanged; no record of the restatus actor/time exists
experiment.interpretation: the theory conflates claim-origin with state-change-origin by having only one provenance carrier

rows.anchor: Lineage IS derivable from K (reachability in R_der) -- this is the one genuinely computable relation in the whole theory (O(n+m)). But Pi and lineage give DIFFERENT answers about origin, and the corpus uses 'provenance' for both in different steps. They must not be conflated.
rows.statement: TEST 3 (a multi-step derivation chain c derives-from b derives-from a0) confirms lineage(c) is computable purely from K's relation set in O(n+m) time -- called the one genuinely computable relation in the whole theory -- but shows Pi(c) ('internal/rule') and lineage(c) (reaching back to the vendor-sourced a0) give different answers about origin, warning the corpus's use of 'provenance' for both must not be conflated.

experiment.hypothesis: lineage (derived via R_der reachability) is computable from K and distinct from Pi (asserted provenance).
experiment.setup: a three-assertion derivation chain a0<-b<-c via derives edges
experiment.assumptions: derives and refers edge types define the lineage reachability relation
experiment.inputs: K3 with a0,b,c and two derives edges
experiment.method: compute lineage(c) and compare to Pi(c)
experiment.result: lineage(c) correctly traces back through b to a0; Pi(c) reports 'internal/rule', an unrelated immediate-origin statement
experiment.interpretation: lineage and provenance answer genuinely different questions about origin
experiment.conclusion: lineage is computable (O(n+m)); it must not be conflated with Pi

rows.anchor: P != A pays off here: independent corroboration is representable as two assertions of one proposition. ANSWERABLE. This is a genuine strength. What is NOT answerable: whether the two sources are INDEPENDENT. The theory has no independence relation -- only R_der (dependence). Absence of a derives-edge is not evidence of independence.
rows.statement: TEST 4 shows two assertions of the same proposition from different sources (vendor, scanner) are correctly representable as two distinct assertions of one proposition (validating P!=A for corroboration), but whether the two sources are genuinely independent is not answerable, since the theory has only a dependence relation (R_der) and no independence relation -- absence of a derives-edge is not evidence of independence, it may simply be unrecorded.
missing: an independence relation on evidence/assertion sources

experiment.hypothesis: K can represent both corroboration (two sources for one proposition) and whether those sources are independent.
experiment.setup: two assertions v (vendor) and s (scanner) of the identical proposition P1
experiment.assumptions: P!=A means the same proposition can be asserted multiple times as distinct assertions
experiment.method: query distinct propositions vs distinct assertions in K4; check for any independence relation
experiment.result: 1 distinct proposition, 2 distinct assertions (corroboration representable); no independence relation exists
experiment.interpretation: corroboration is representable but independence-of-sources is not
experiment.conclusion: ANSWERABLE for corroboration; NOT ANSWERABLE for independence

rows.anchor: Assertion provenance survives merge (Step 265 s265.11 'merge test' PASSES). MERGE provenance does not exist: the merge event itself has no record inside K. Two different merge orders producing the same K are indistinguishable -- and EXP-10b showed those orders can produce DIFFERENT K under a latest-wins rule, so the unrecorded order is semantically load-bearing.
rows.statement: TEST 5 confirms Step 265 s265.11's merge test passes (assertion-level provenance survives a merge, distinguishable via Pi.source), but shows the merge event itself (when it happened, who authorized it) has no record inside K at all; cross-references EXP-10b's finding that different merge orders can produce different K under a latest-wins rule, meaning the unrecorded merge order is semantically load-bearing information that is silently lost.
missing: a record of the merge event: when, by whom, in what order

lineage_claims.quote: Assertion provenance survives merge (Step 265 s265.11 'merge test' PASSES).
EXP-10b showed those orders can produce DIFFERENT K under a latest-wins rule, so the unrecorded order is semantically load-bearing.

rows.anchor: The three ANSWERABLE questions are exactly PROVENANCE and LINEAGE. The four unanswerable ones are exactly HISTORY. CONCLUSION (executed): Provenance and Lineage belong to the STATE; History does NOT reduce to the state, and Step 247's K_t=(K_t,H_t) is therefore NECESSARY, not merely convenient.
rows.statement: TEST 6, the decisive test: two different histories (H_a: assert(v); H_b: assert(s), assert(v), withdraw(scanner)) replay to structurally-equal states K(H_a)=K(H_b); of seven audit-relevant questions posed against K alone, exactly the three that are provenance/lineage questions (current state, origin of each assertion, derivation) are answerable, and exactly the four history-dependent questions (was anything withdrawn, was anything contradicted, how many revisions, who withdrew a source) are not; concludes Provenance and Lineage belong to the state K, while History does not reduce to K, making Step 247's meta-structure script-K_t=(K_t,H_t) a mathematical necessity rather than a mere convenience.

lineage_claims.quote: Step 247's K_t=(K_t,H_t) is therefore NECESSARY, not merely convenient.

experiment.hypothesis: K1=K2 (structural equality) is a sufficient basis for auditing whether the underlying histories were the same, i.e. History reduces to K.
experiment.setup: two constructed histories H_a and H_b, replayed to Ka and Kb respectively
experiment.assumptions: replay is deterministic (fold of T over the operation sequence)
experiment.method: compare Ka, Kb structurally; then answer seven audit-relevant questions from K alone and classify each answerable/not
experiment.result: Ka and Kb are structurally equal; 3 of 7 questions (state, provenance, lineage) answerable; 4 (withdrawal, contradiction, revision count, who-withdrew) not answerable
experiment.interpretation: History carries information not recoverable from K, so a meta-structure combining K and H is necessary for a complete audit
experiment.conclusion: History does NOT reduce to the state; script-K_t=(K_t,H_t) is necessary

rows.anchor: Provenance != Lineage is established and matters: Pi(c) = <internal/rule@2> while lineage(c) = [a0, b] and a0's origin is vendor. The two give different answers about "where did this come from," and the corpus uses the word provenance for both in different steps.
rows.statement: Restates and formalizes the Provenance-vs-Lineage distinction with a concrete worked example (Pi(c)=internal/rule@2 vs lineage(c)=[a0,b] tracing back to a vendor origin), warning the corpus's use of the single word 'provenance' for both meanings is a live source of confusion.

rows.anchor: The questions answerable from K are EXACTLY provenance and lineage. The questions that are not are EXACTLY history. Therefore Step 247's K_t = (K_t, H_t) is necessary, not merely convenient. The corpus derives this by argument at Step 247 and then, from Step 262 onward, drops H from the terminal model ... Execution says the demotion costs four audit-relevant questions.
rows.statement: Finding PL-6, called the central result of the document: the six-test placement matrix shows exactly two of eight audit-relevant concepts (assertion provenance, lineage) are answerable from K alone, while transition provenance, merge provenance, withdrawal record, contestation record, evidence provenance, and source-independence are not; concludes Step 247's meta-structure K_t=(K_t,H_t) is mathematically necessary, and criticizes the corpus for deriving this necessity by argument at Step 247 and then silently dropping H from the terminal model from Step 262 onward (relegating history to 'external'), a demotion shown by execution to cost exactly four audit-relevant questions.

rows.anchor: ## E. What SURVIVED — the load-bearing positives
rows.statement: Sixteen results are registered as SURVIVED and load-bearing for any successor theory, including: provenance must be carried not derived (S-01); lineage is computable in O(n+m), the one unambiguously decidable relation in the theory (S-02); 𝒦=(K,H) is necessary, 4 audit questions unanswerable from K alone (S-03); Evidence(O,P,C,R) is a relation not a substance (S-04); admission≠truth (S-05); P≠A makes independent corroboration representable (S-06); no scalar operator suffices for evidence aggregation (S-08); K=(𝒜,ℛ) is instantiated and running — 40 assertions, 59 typed relations (S-12); two orthogonal status axes are running and schema-enforced (S-13); a real constitutional self-amendment rule exists (S-14).

rows.anchor: TEST 1  Imported assertion at t=0
rows.statement: TEST 1: at t=0 an imported assertion's provenance is answerable from K alone (<vendor/import@0>) but its history is not (K carries no H, so 'imported at t=0' is indistinguishable from 'asserted at t=0 by a person'); this confirms by construction Step 265 §265.2's base-case argument that provenance must be carried, not derived from an empty history — the strongest single argument in Step 265.

rows.anchor: TEST 3  Multi-step derivation
rows.statement: TEST 3: lineage (reachability in R_der) is derivable from K alone and is the one genuinely computable relation in the whole theory (O(n+m)), but Π and lineage give different answers about an assertion's origin (Π says 'internal/rule', lineage traces to the ultimate vendor source) and the corpus uses 'provenance' for both in different steps — they must not be conflated.

rows.anchor: TEST 6  Identical current states, different histories  -- the decisive test
rows.statement: TEST 6 (decisive): two histories (H_a: assert(v); H_b: assert(s); assert(v); withdraw(scanner)) produce structurally identical current states K(H_a)=K(H_b)=['v']. From K alone, three questions are answerable (what does K say now; where did each assertion come from; what is each derived from — exactly PROVENANCE and LINEAGE) and four are not (was anything ever withdrawn; was this claim ever contradicted; how many times revised; who withdrew the scanner source — exactly HISTORY). Conclusion: Provenance and Lineage belong to the state; History does not reduce to the state; therefore Step 247's 𝒦_t=(K_t,H_t) is necessary, not merely convenient.

experiment.hypothesis: K=(A,R) alone (without a separate history component H) is a sufficient state for governance-relevant audit questions
experiment.setup: two histories H_a and H_b that produce structurally identical final states
experiment.assumptions: the 7 listed questions represent what 'a real audit asks'
experiment.inputs: H_a, H_b and the resulting K(H_a), K(H_b)
experiment.method: answer each of 7 audit questions using only the final state K, for both histories
experiment.result: 3 of 7 questions answerable from K alone (provenance, lineage-related); 4 are not (withdrawal, contestation, revision count, who-withdrew)
experiment.interpretation: the 4 unanswerable questions are exactly the class HISTORY names; K alone cannot answer them regardless of which history produced it
experiment.limitations: one constructed pair of histories, though the four-question gap is structural not incidental
experiment.conclusion: 𝒦=(K,H) is necessary, not merely convenient, confirming Step 247

sources.note: A read-only, warn-only mechanical checker capability (structural profile S1-S5, back-tested against historical migration-plan states) plus an author-side handoff-report adoption (S0143, S0144, S0148), explicitly bounded to declared-structure checks only.

rows.anchor: the five realized S1–S5 structural checks are run over the migration plan as it stood at each historical commit and must reproduce the defects the independent reviews raised — and must be QUIET on the repaired current artifact
rows.statement: A falsification back-test materializes three historical git states of the migration plan (AMD4/AMD5/AMD6 commits) and runs five realized structural checks (S1-S5) over each; the matrix correctly reproduces the historical defects (DI-1, DI-2, DI-5, DI-7, DI-4) at the states where independent reviewers found them and is quiet (never falsely PASS) on the corrected AMD6 state.

experiment.hypothesis: A deterministic mechanical checker (S1-S5) can rediscover the mechanical defect classes independent human reviewers found across the AMD3-AMD6 migration-plan chain, and remain quiet on the corrected artifact.
experiment.setup: Each historical commit of the migration plan is materialized read-only via git show; byte-verified against known line counts (706/833/1206).
experiment.assumptions: The historical defects are purely mechanical/structural (identifier collisions, dangling references, stale vocabulary, confusable identifiers, unlabelled superseded text) and thus checkable without architectural judgement.
experiment.inputs: Three git commits of the migration plan (AMD4 0a2fa71d, AMD5 7d3abc59, AMD6 8307beca).
experiment.method: Run S1 (identifier-check), S2 (link-check anchors), S3 (vocabulary/confusable check), S4 (table-shape check), S5 (superseded-labelling check) over each historical state and the current state.
experiment.result: AMD4: S1/S2/S3 FAIL with exact evidence matching DI-1/DI-2; AMD5: S2/S3 FAIL matching DI-5/DI-7, S5 WARN matching DI-4; AMD6: all PASS or documented INCONCLUSIVE, 0 false positives.
experiment.interpretation: The checker is content-driven and the regression direction holds: it fires on defective states and is silent on the repaired one.
experiment.limitations: Two required target classes (enumeration-vs-content agreement; R-CONFLICT sequence/grant-identity checks) are explicitly NOT-CHECKED because no catalogued capability owns them yet.
experiment.conclusion: PASS for the authorized Phase-0 scope only; a PASS here is mechanical, not architectural, assurance.

rows.anchor: mechanical assurance proves DECLARED STRUCTURE — identifier uniqueness, intra-document reference resolution, declared vocabulary, table shape, disposition labelling. It does NOT check soundness, completeness, authority, or provenance
rows.statement: The D-4 statement, carried verbatim on every report: mechanical assurance proves declared structure only; it cannot discover an undeclared architectural act (the missing-act class, e.g. RD-1, RD-7, RD-3·b), which is caught only by human Architecture review — 'a PASS here is mechanical, not architectural, assurance.'

rows.anchor: DI-3/DI-6 enumeration-vs-content agreement ... NOT-CHECKED. No catalogued capability owns the class. Named as OQ-1 and returned to Governance/ARB
rows.statement: A required back-test target (a stated count contradicting the rows it counts, e.g. DI-3/DI-6) is deliberately NOT built because no catalogued capability owns that class of check; the gap is returned to governance as an open question rather than an ad-hoc capability being invented to close it.

rows.anchor: copy the clean (AMD6) artifact, introduce ONE defect per copy, run the adapter over the directory ... every verdict flipped, with correct line evidence, and unmutated copies stayed PASS
rows.statement: A mutation-testing methodology (one injected defect per otherwise-clean artifact copy) is used to demonstrate the checkers are content-driven rather than canned: a single heading collision produces both a direct S1 duplicate-identifier failure and a cascading S2 reference-ambiguity failure across ~20 citation sites, an added dangling step reference correctly triggers S2, a dropped table cell correctly triggers S4, and unmutated control copies stay PASS in every slice.

experiment.hypothesis: The structural checkers (S1-S5) respond to actual document content rather than being hard-coded to expect specific known-good/known-bad files.
experiment.setup: Copy the clean, corrected (AMD6) migration-plan artifact into a temp directory three times; introduce exactly one synthetic defect into each copy.
experiment.assumptions: A checker that is content-driven will flip verdict on the mutated copy and remain PASS on an untouched control copy of the same artifact.
experiment.inputs: Three mutated copies (heading collision, added dangling step reference, dropped table cell) plus unmutated controls.
experiment.method: Run the adapters (knowledge-lint, link-check, identifier-check) over each mutated copy and each control copy; compare verdicts and cited evidence lines.
experiment.result: Every mutation produced the expected FAIL with correct line-numbered evidence; the heading-collision mutation additionally produced a second-order reference-ambiguity failure; all controls stayed PASS.
experiment.interpretation: The checkers are genuinely reading and evaluating content, not merely returning canned results for known files.
experiment.limitations: Tests only three specific mutation classes; does not test every defect class the checkers claim to cover.
experiment.conclusion: CONFORMS — Phase 0 is implemented, works, and is content-driven, proved by mutation rather than by reading the code.

rows.anchor: V-2 ... FIVE LIVE TRUE POSITIVES, and they had survived every review that passed over them ... The implementation design passed the Governance review and three independent Architecture reviews with a malformed table in it.
rows.statement: Running the checker over already-reviewed governed documents (not test fixtures) surfaces five real, previously-uncaught table-shape defects, including one in the implementation-design document that had already passed a Governance review and three independent Architecture reviews — the program's first operational evidence not obtained via a back-test.

rows.anchor: V-3 ... S2 CANNOT DISTINGUISH DEFINING an enumeration from QUOTING one — a systematic false-positive class over review artifacts ... this very verification report ... it parsed an enumeration I QUOTED as one I DEFINED
rows.statement: Measuring the S2 reference-check over 83 review documents finds 9 false-positive FAILs (including all four AMD architecture reviews and this very verification report, which misread its own quoted enumeration as a defining one), because S2 cannot yet distinguish a document that DEFINES an enumeration from one that merely CITES/QUOTES it — a rule-scope gap to be raised as an open question, not silently suppressed.
missing: a mechanism to distinguish defining vs. citing documents

rows.anchor: V-4 ... EKS-06 IS ALREADY TAKEN — and the brainstorming document still assumes it is free ... a live DP-1/PMR-10 collision waiting to happen.
rows.statement: An identifier EKS-06 was minted for one problem (reference resolution) at 14:35 the same day, while a separate brainstorming document and its review both independently propose 'EKS-06' for a different problem (governance-assurance/role-execution scaling); the mint is also uncommitted (invisible to git and to any collision check), constituting a live identifier-collision risk.

rows.anchor: Mechanical Assurance proves DECLARED STRUCTURE / Architecture Review discovers UNDECLARED ARCHITECTURAL CONTENT.
rows.statement: An addendum records the Decision Authority's own refinement of the mechanical/architectural boundary, framing it as a division of labour rather than a limitation, and explicitly forbidding the platform from ever claiming 'mechanical assurance proves architectural completeness.'

lineage_claims.quote: This is a better formulation than X-5's and it should be the platform's standing sentence

rows.anchor: nine required elements ... aggregate verdict: [FAIL] — fail-closed, never PASS on silence
rows.statement: Defines a nine-element handoff assurance report (artifact identity, checker/version/commit, checks executed, aggregate result, findings-with-evidence, evidence locations, NOT-CHECKED areas, known limitations, timestamp/execution context) with a fail-closed aggregate-verdict precedence rule FAIL > INCONCLUSIVE > WARN > PASS, discovered and repaired as a CLI-test finding during implementation (an INCONCLUSIVE slice preceding a FAIL could otherwise mask it).

rows.anchor: AMD4 ... FAIL ... AMD5 ... FAIL ... AMD6 ... INCONCLUSIVE ... New authoring draft ... FAIL ... Same draft, remediated ... INCONCLUSIVE
rows.statement: Real-corpus validation of the author-side handoff report across five runs (defective AMD4, defective AMD5, corrected AMD6 without a vocabulary config, a fresh defective authoring draft, and the same draft remediated) shows the expected fail/pass pattern in every case, with the tool refusing PASS even after remediation on slices it cannot fully assess (fail-closed by construction), and zero false positives on the corrected AMD6 state.

rows.anchor: OBSERVED (measured in the record, cited) ... ESTIMATED (clearly labelled — not measured) ... UNKNOWN (not measured, not invented)
rows.statement: Business-value reporting discipline: claims are strictly separated into OBSERVED (measured, cited), ESTIMATED (explicitly labelled as an estimate derived from observed chain volume, e.g. 'per-defect cost is closer to one amendment cycle than one reviewer minute'), and UNKNOWN (explicitly not measured and not invented, e.g. reviewer-hour or financial savings, or whether authors will voluntarily run a warn-only checker).

rows.anchor: KOS-AIP-GOV-STATE-DURABILITY should be the FIRST real consumer of the deterministic assurance capability — not a second project that waits until durability is finished.
rows.statement: Recommends that the durability migration work become the first real consumer of the deterministic assurance capability rather than a separate, sequential project, arguing the two tracks already share an evidence base (the migration corpus is the checker's own back-test corpus), making integration a sequencing/authority problem rather than a new architecture problem.

rows.statement: States the one load-bearing coupling rule between the two tracks: the assurance checker's root-resolution mechanism must follow wherever the governed evidence boundary is placed by B', never define or own that boundary itself, so ownership of the boundary stays exclusively with the durability decision.
invariants: Assurance root resolution must FOLLOW the governed evidence boundary; it must not DEFINE or OWN that boundary.
