sources.note: Step 70's minimal-kernel derivation via explicit removal-testing (each of eight primitives shown necessary by a FAIL-on-removal experiment, State shown operationally-but-not-logically necessary), the Logical-vs-Operational kernel split, Provider≠Authority with an explicit kernel-exclusion list, the Design-by-Contract transformation schema, the I_CompositionalProvenance invariant, atomicity/transaction bridging, event partial-ordering (Ordering≠Causality), and the hexagonal Core+Ports+Adapters architecture. Distinct methodologically from kos-primitive-reduction-kernel (Step 49, abstract mathematical reduction) though converging on a similar primitive set.

rows.anchor: Kernel hypothesis K_OS=(A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R); goal is the smallest trusted kernel, not a maximal platform
rows.statement: States the goal: the smallest executable system preserving all established mathematical properties, warning against building a huge platform containing every discussed concept. Proposes the candidate kernel K_OS = (A,T,P,E,I,S,X,R): Artifact, Epistemic Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, State, Transformation, Rule/Policy.

rows.anchor: Eight removal experiments each yield FAIL, demonstrating each primitive is necessary
rows.statement: Removal experiment 1 (Artifact identity): two identical claims C1=C2=p without identity make it impossible to determine which downstream decisions depended on which instance after one is invalidated -- FAIL, confirming ArtifactIdentity is fundamental. Experiment 2 (Type): content with no semantic type lets another process interpret 'system will fail tomorrow' as Fact with no way to detect illegitimacy -- FAIL, confirming Type is a kernel primitive. Experiment 3 (Provenance): ten agents producing the same statement without provenance yield an uninspectable SupportCount=10 -- FAIL, confirming provenance is indispensable. Experiment 4 (Event): knowledge changing from p to not-p with no recorded event leaves 'why did it change' Unknown -- FAIL, confirming event history is necessary for high-integrity evolution. Experiment 5 (Invariant): without invariant checking, P(A)=1.4 is structurally accepted -- FAIL, confirming Invariant must be executable. Experiment 8 (Policy): a decision auto-executing with no authorization rule -- FAIL, confirming governance policy belongs in the computational architecture (numbered out of sequence with experiments 7 and 9 in the source, which concern Transformation and Provider authority respectively).

experiment.hypothesis: Each of Artifact, Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, and Policy is individually necessary for the kernel -- removing any one produces a demonstrable architectural failure.
experiment.setup: Five removal experiments (70.4, 70.6, 70.8, 70.10, 70.12) plus the Policy removal experiment (70.18).
experiment.assumptions: The other kernel primitives remain present while the tested one is removed.
experiment.inputs: Six scenario premises as summarized in the statement.
experiment.method: Remove one candidate primitive and check whether a previously-required architectural property (identity tracing, type safety, independence accounting, change explanation, range validity, authorization) can still be maintained.
experiment.result: All six removal experiments FAIL (the property cannot be maintained without the primitive).
experiment.interpretation: Artifact, Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, and Policy are each individually necessary, non-redundant kernel primitives.
experiment.limitations: Manual scenario construction, not an exhaustive removal search over all primitive combinations.
experiment.conclusion: Removal experiments for Artifact, Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, Policy: all FAIL as expected, confirming necessity.

rows.anchor: State-projection removal experiment: PASS WITH PERFORMANCE FAILURE -- State is operationally, not logically, fundamental
rows.statement: Notes State S_t can theoretically be reconstructed as a projection of event history S_t = Pi(E_1:t), so it is not necessarily fundamental in the mathematical sense. Experiment 6: storing millions of events with no efficient state projection makes every query require a complete replay -- theoretically computable but operationally inefficient -- 'PASS WITH PERFORMANCE FAILURE', concluding StateProjection is operationally necessary even though not logically fundamental.

rows.anchor: Explicit-transformation and provider-authority removal experiments (implicit conversion and auto-verified LLM output both FAIL)
rows.statement: Experiment 7: the system directly converting Prediction into Fact with no transformation record -- FAIL, confirming transformations must be explicit. Experiment 9: an LLM-produced Claim being automatically assigned Authority=Verified -- FAIL, confirming the provider must remain separate from epistemic authority.

rows.anchor: Logical kernel K_L=(A,T,P,E,I,X,R) vs Operational kernel K_O=K_L+StateProjection+Indexes+Caching
rows.statement: Having confirmed all eight primitives survive removal testing, freezes the candidate kernel K_OS = Artifact+Type+Provenance+Event+Invariant+State+Transformation+Policy, then refines the distinction between logical and implementation primitives: State is reconstructible from Events (not fundamental mathematically) but operationally valuable, giving Logical kernel K_L=(A,T,P,E,I,X,R) versus Operational kernel K_O = K_L + StateProjection + Indexes + Caching.

lineage_claims.quote: K_OS = Artifact + Type + Provenance + Event + Invariant + State + Transformation + Policy.

rows.anchor: Trusted-kernel-smaller-than-the-platform principle; explicit exclusion list; Provider != Authority
rows.statement: States the critical DDD principle: the trusted kernel should be smaller than the platform surrounding it -- AI systems, databases, graph engines, search engines, and statistical libraries should not all become part of the trusted semantic kernel. Explicitly excludes from the kernel, at least initially: VectorSearch, LLM, Embedding, PromptManagement, SpecificDatabaseTechnology, SpecificCloudProvider, SpecificAgentFramework -- these are replaceable computational providers, giving Provider != Authority (an LLM may provide a Hypothesis but gains no authority to declare VerifiedFact). Warns that a kernel dependent on one LLM or VectorDB becomes technology-bound, violating 'domain semantics dominate infrastructure'.

rows.anchor: Kernel API sketch; Design-by-Contract transformation schema X=(InputType,OutputType,Preconditions,Procedure,Postconditions,ProvenanceRule)
rows.statement: Sketches a conceptual kernel API (observe(), measure(), registerArtifact(), transform(), validate(), derive(), recordEvent(), queryProvenance(), evaluatePolicy(), authorize()) -- exact API left undesigned but semantic primitives clarified. Formalizes a transformation as X=(InputType, OutputType, Preconditions, Procedure, Postconditions, ProvenanceRule), 'much stronger than a generic function'; example: Measurement->Evidence with Preconditions=ValidUnit∧ValidSource∧ValidTimestamp and Postcondition=EvidenceHasProvenance. Experiment 10: an invalid-unit measurement attempted through Measurement->Evidence is Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 11: a transformation that creates an Evidence object but loses its source yields TransformationInvalid -- PASS, resembling Design by Contract (Precondition + Transformation + Postcondition), 'extremely suitable for deterministic assurance'.

rows.anchor: Composition requires Post(X1)⇒Pre(X2) and type match; new invariant I_CompositionalProvenance
rows.statement: For X1:T1->T2 and X2:T2->T3, X2∘X1:T1->T3 is valid only if Post(X1)⇒Pre(X2). Experiment 12: composing X1 (Prediction->Claim) with X2 (Evidence->Decision) fails on type mismatch -- CompositionError -- PASS, showing the architecture is composable without one giant reasoning algorithm. Requires provenance to compose too: if e=V(m) and c=I(e), then Anc(c) superset-of Anc(e) union {m}. Experiment 13: two individually valid transformations whose composition loses the original measurement reference yields CompositionInvalid -- PASS, giving the new invariant I_CompositionalProvenance: valid transformations must preserve required ancestry across composition -- 'extremely important for AI pipelines'.
invariants: I_CompositionalProvenance: valid transformations must preserve required ancestry across composition

rows.anchor: Atomicity/transaction-boundary bridging mathematical invariants to software invariants
rows.statement: Notes a transformation producing Artifact+Event+Provenance could be partially committed, risking ArtifactExists but ProvenanceMissing -- dangerous. Requires Artifact+Event+RequiredProvenance to commit as one atomic, consistent transition. Experiment 14: a database failure between artifact creation and provenance persistence should yield TransactionRollback or RecoverableIncompleteState, never silently appearing valid -- PASS. States the bridge explicitly: the mathematical invariant Provenance(a)!=empty becomes a database/transaction requirement -- 'Mathematical invariant -> Software invariant... the bridge we were looking for'.
invariants: Provenance(a) ≠ empty is enforced as an atomic transaction requirement, never a partially-committable side effect

rows.anchor: Event identity and partial (not invented total) ordering; Ordering != Causality
rows.statement: Requires events to have identity id(e) and ordering semantics e_i≺e_j where relevant, noting a distributed system may lack a global total order, requiring a PartialOrder instead (e.g. e1≺e3 and e2≺e3 without e1≺e2). Experiment 15: two causally-unordered distributed events should not have an invented e1<e2 -- OrderingUncertain -- PASS, relevant when integrating Git/Jira/CI/production telemetry/human decisions/AI outputs with differing clocks (Timestamp != CausalOrder). Notes a Lamport-style logical clock establishes e1->e2 only when causality is actually known; L(e1)<L(e2) does not mean e1 caused e2 -- Ordering != Causality. Experiment 16: an agent claiming Cause(e1,e2) purely from L(e1)<L(e2) is Rejected -- PASS.

lineage_claims.quote: Ordering ≠ Causality.

rows.anchor: Hexagonal kernel architecture; AI-provider and database-technology replacement preserve core invariants
rows.statement: Depicts the kernel (Artifact, Epistemic Type, Provenance, Event, Invariant, Transformation, Policy, State Projection) surrounded by AI/ML Engine, Statistics, Causal Engine, and External Systems -- 'very close to Hexagonal Architecture' (Core + Ports + Adapters: LLMAdapter, GitAdapter, JiraAdapter, DatabaseAdapter, StatisticalEngineAdapter), with the domain kernel not depending on concrete technologies. Experiment 17: replacing LLM_A with LLM_B leaves KnowledgeOS epistemic semantics unchanged -- CoreInvariantPreserved -- PASS. Experiment 18: replacing relational storage with another storage implementation leaves KnowledgeOSCore behaving equivalently as long as semantic contracts hold -- PASS, demonstrating architectural independence from infrastructure.

rows.anchor: Kernel execution loop; AI as computational participant not epistemic authority; KnowledgeOS = Governed Semantic Kernel + Computational Providers
rows.statement: Defines the minimal executable kernel loop Input -> Classify -> Validate -> Transform -> CheckInvariants -> Commit -> ProjectState, worked through a Measurement->Evidence example, and notes an AI (e.g. for Evidence->Hypothesis) may perform generation while the kernel still controls InputType, OutputType, Provenance, Policy, Persistence -- 'AI is a computational participant, not the epistemic authority', 'probably one of the most important architectural conclusions so far'. Concludes KnowledgeOS should not be designed as LLM+Memory but as Governed Semantic Kernel + Computational Providers, with the LLM one provider among several. States the kernel's basic operations are O(n)/O(n log n) for practical cases, with LLM/large-scale statistics/causal models/massive data processing as optional providers -- 'KnowledgeOS does not inherently require large-scale infrastructure'.

rows.anchor: Step 70 verdict: minimal kernel as a credible software architecture target; opens Step 71 on compositional correctness
rows.statement: Declares STEP 70 -- PASS: a minimal kernel requires typed artifacts, provenance, explicit transformations, eventual state, executable invariants, and policy-controlled transitions, with everything else composable around it -- 'the mathematics can be compiled into a small set of executable semantic contracts'. Describes the current architecture as KnowledgeOS = SemanticKernel + KnowledgeGraph + InferenceEngines + AI Agents + Governance + External Adapters, with the Semantic Kernel as the trusted center. Poses the remaining question of whether a sequence of individually valid transformations remains valid when composed into a large workflow (Valid(X1) and Valid(X2) do not automatically imply Valid(X2∘X1)), opening Step 71 (Compositional Correctness of KnowledgeOS, already covered as S0968) to examine ContractComposition, InvariantComposition, ProvenanceComposition, TransactionComposition, WorkflowCorrectness, and AgentComposition.

rows.statement: knowledge-types.yaml is confirmed as a documentation ontology, not a hybrid: types like 'aggregate' or 'event' look like domain objects but their own descriptions are documentary ('aggregate' = a single aggregate's design, invariants, and boundary; 'event' = a domain event's payload/producers/consumers) — these are documents about domain objects, not the domain objects themselves.

rows.anchor: Ontology layers — THREE, not four ... a fourth layer is therefore declined ... L-A EXISTS · EXECUTABLE · ENFORCED ... L-B DOES NOT EXIST ... L-C PARTIALLY EXISTS ... "Engineering Knowledge Ontology" NOT EVIDENCED AS A SEPARATE LAYER
rows.statement: Three ontology layers are recognized, per the commission's own rule (do not invent new layers unless repository evidence requires them): L-A Documentation Ontology exists, executable, enforced (31 types x 8 statuses x 5 authorities x 9 audiences x 12 contexts x 11 edges, 18 lint rules, a generated graph); L-B Platform Ontology does not exist (D-1..D-7 is its seed); L-C Product Ontology partially exists (bounded-contexts.yaml plus unindexed Round29 catalogs). A proposed fourth 'Engineering Knowledge Ontology' middle layer is declined as not evidenced separately: knowledge-types.yaml already covers engineering-knowledge kinds (adr, ddd-discovery, research, review, playbook, checklist, template, decision, quality) — L-A is the engineering-knowledge ontology, at document granularity.

rows.anchor: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in the existing schemas ... KEY COLLISION — mechanical, not aesthetic
rows.statement: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in knowledge-types.yaml or bounded-contexts.yaml: (1) key collision, mechanical and decisive — bounded-contexts.yaml already contains a 'governance' key (product-side, code_path app/Contexts/Governance), so adding D-1 'Engineering Governance' would collide with an existing key in a lint-enforced enum; (2) vocabulary insufficiency, strong — the domain model's verbs (governs, produces, consumes, validates, derives, depends on, observes) have no expression in the edge vocabulary (depends_on, derived_from, verified_by), which lacks governs/produces/consumes/observes; (3) subject mismatch, strong — every L-A field is a property of a document (knowledge_id, last_review, code_refs), but 'Engineering Method' has no reviewer, next-review date, or code refs, so it cannot carry a knowledge card. Verdict: D-1..D-7 belong to L-B (which does not yet exist); expressing them as data would require a separate vocabulary file with its own enum namespace, an ARB decision.

rows.anchor: The five commissioned deliverables ... L-B ↔ L-A relationship | L-B would OWN and CLASSIFY L-A; L-A would never contain L-B
rows.statement: L-B would own and classify L-A, never the reverse: L-A's subject is the document, L-B's subject is the platform — one is the metadata of artifacts, the other the architecture of the thing that produces them. The executable ontology should not change to accommodate L-B; two separately-warranted, ARB-only changes exist: whether scope.include should extend beyond docs/knowledge/** (a declared-scope amendment, not a bug fix), and whether the edge vocabulary needs governs/produces/consumes/observes, answerable only after L-B exists.

sources.note: The evidentiary-discipline tagging scheme used throughout the B0030-B0040 verification/phase_measure_theory steps to prevent hypothetical scenarios from being promoted to proven counterexamples or results.

rows.anchor: We use: PROVEN ... EXECUTED ... CORPUS-ESTABLISHED ... CONDITIONAL ... CANDIDATE ... UNRESOLVED
rows.statement: Evidentiary discipline for this verification phase: every claimed result must be tagged PROVEN (follows formally from established definitions/theorems), EXECUTED (actually instantiated and evaluated), CORPUS-ESTABLISHED (supported directly by corpus evidence), CONDITIONAL (valid only under explicit stated assumptions), CANDIDATE (proposed test, not yet demonstrated), or UNRESOLVED (insufficient evidence); hypothetical counterexamples must never be counted as proven counterexamples.

rows.anchor: My first policy demonstration was degenerate. Assess(A1,'default') and Assess(A1,'two-source') both returned ('Supporting','Weak') ... The demonstration failed to show what I claimed. I replaced it with a discriminating pair (strict-provenance) ... The original output is retained above rather than d
rows.statement: Self-disclosed methodological failure: the first attempt to demonstrate policy-sensitivity of Assess used a non-discriminating policy pair (default vs two-source), which returned identical results at both n=1 and n=2 and therefore failed to show the intended point; it was replaced with a genuinely discriminating pair (strict-provenance), and the original failed output was deliberately retained rather than deleted, in keeping with the programme's evidentiary transparency discipline.

rows.statement: Second self-disclosed methodological failure: an initial EKP parse reported 51 dangling endpoints (an artifact of markdown-bracket syntax), then a corrected parse still reported 1 (an artifact of a glob excluding a .yaml package file that the real linter does scan); the platform's own knowledge-lint tool correctly reports zero errors; both false positives are explicitly disclosed rather than silently fixed, on the stated principle that a verification programme that hides its own false positives is not one.

rows.statement: The corpus's own executable reference implementation of the step-42 admissibility law is run directly and passes five distinct checks (no-averaging, Unknown-invariant-blocks, epistemic-pass/auth-fail, auth-pass/hard-invariant-fail, safety-critical-unknown-always-blocks); independence from the verifier's own work is confirmed via a contamination check — ten fingerprints unique to the verifier's own artifacts are searched for in the file with zero hits, and the file's modification time (2026-08-28 23:51) predates the verifier's findings, establishing it as genuinely INDEPENDENT CORPUS EVIDENCE rather than something the verifier itself introduced.

experiment.hypothesis: the corpus's step-42 admissibility law is already implemented and independent of the verifier's own work
experiment.setup: locate and run ladder_dc_reference.py; search it for ten fingerprints unique to the verifier's own artifacts
experiment.assumptions: a genuine fingerprint match would indicate contamination (the verifier's own prior work leaking into 'corpus' evidence)
experiment.inputs: the reference file's source and mtime
experiment.method: execute the five test cases; grep for the ten fingerprints
experiment.result: all five checks pass; zero fingerprint hits; file predates the verifier's findings
experiment.interpretation: the evaluation law is independently corpus-established and executable, not verifier-invented
experiment.limitations: ten fingerprints is a finite, chosen set

rows.anchor: We must not upgrade this immediately to a universal theorem. ... VERIFIED: provenance cannot universally be derived from History(T). ... DERIVED/RECOMMENDED: store a stable provenance reference in K. ... rather than: PROVEN: full provenance object belongs in K.
rows.statement: Explicit evidentiary-discipline caution against overclaiming: the step's actual epistemic status is VERIFIED that provenance cannot universally be derived from History(T), and DERIVED/RECOMMENDED that a stable provenance reference should be stored in K — carefully distinguished from the stronger, unearned claim that the full provenance object is PROVEN to belong in K; whether every KnowledgeOS deployment requires provenance as part of semantic state identity remains a separate, open question.

rows.anchor: CORPUS ESTABLISHES / FORMALLY DERIVED / EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED / IMPLEMENTED / PROPOSED / UNRESOLVED / REFUTED. Never collapse these classes.
rows.statement: A seven-value evidence-classification vocabulary is mandated for the dependency-audit stage (CORPUS ESTABLISHES, FORMALLY DERIVED, EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED, PROPOSED, UNRESOLVED, REFUTED), a variant of the evidentiary discipline used elsewhere in the programme, with an explicit instruction to never collapse the classes into one another.

sources.note: A structural role taxonomy (Source/Teacher, Questioner/Learner, Recipient, Transmitter, Custodian, Practitioner/Actor, Authority/Governor) abstracted from Bhagavad Gita Chapter 4 characters (Krishna, Arjuna, Vivasvan, Manu, Ikshvaku, Rajarsis), used as a pre-analogy structural analysis before mapping onto KnowledgeOS architecture; continues the same Gita-as-validation-lens thread as gita-chapter3-validation-exercise but is chapter-4-specific.

rows.anchor: Before Step 158, it is useful to pause and summarize Chapter 4 itself, especially its actors and their roles. We should not yet force the architecture analogy onto it.
rows.statement: The author deliberately defers forcing an architecture analogy onto Gita Chapter 4 until the text's actual actors/roles/propositions are established first, as a methodological discipline against premature mapping.

rows.anchor: Krishna therefore occupies several roles simultaneously: Teacher, Source of the teaching, Interpreter of the teaching, Explainer of its historical transmission, Respondent to Arjuna's questions, Exemplar of action without attachment, Authority explaining when and why the teaching is restored
rows.statement: Krishna is analyzed as simultaneously occupying multiple roles (Teacher, Source, Interpreter, Explainer-of-transmission, Respondent, Exemplar, Authority) rather than being reducible to a single 'knowledge repository' role; he is explicitly characterized as an active teacher and interlocutor, not a passive store.

rows.anchor: Arjuna detects a temporal inconsistency ... Krishna's apparent birth < Vivasvan's antiquity ... And therefore asks for clarification. That makes Arjuna an important epistemic actor in Chapter 4.
rows.statement: Arjuna is cast as Questioner/Skeptic/Recipient/Interlocutor/Verifier-through-questioning/Learner: he detects a temporal inconsistency in Krishna's claim of having taught Vivasvan (since Krishna appears younger than Vivasvan) and demands clarification, making him a structurally important epistemic-verification actor rather than a passive recipient.

rows.anchor: Krishna -> Vivasvan -> Manu -> Ikshvaku ... Rajarsis ... subsequent tradition
rows.statement: Formalizes the named transmission lineage as a directed chain Krishna -> Vivasvan -> Manu -> Ikshvaku -> Rajarsis -> subsequent tradition, with each intermediate node (Vivasvan, Manu) playing a dual Receiver->Transmitter role, distinct from the separate Questioner<->Teacher inquiry link (Arjuna<->Krishna).

rows.anchor: Rajarsis ... They represent people who combine: Royal responsibility + Spiritual/epistemic knowledge. So the transmission is not presented merely as: teacher -> scholar but as something entering the domain of responsible action and governance.
rows.statement: The Rajarsis (royal sages) role is distinguished as combining royal/governance responsibility with epistemic knowledge, meaning the teaching's transmission is framed as entering the domain of responsible action and governance rather than remaining purely academic (teacher->scholar).

rows.anchor: Krishna explains that whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, he manifests himself ... This is not another human character. It is a role/function attributed to Krishna himself. So we should not create a separate "character" called "Avatar" in our architectural analysis.
rows.statement: Explicitly rules the divine-manifestation/avatar theme out as a separate 'character' in the architectural analogy: it is instead modeled as a role/function chain attributed to Krishna himself (Krishna -> Teacher -> Incarnational agent -> Restorer of Dharma), warning against reifying a function as a new actor.

rows.anchor: If we want the minimal actor model for our next architectural comparison, I would retain these seven: 1. Source/Teacher 2. Questioner/Learner 3. Recipient 4. Transmitter 5. Custodian 6. Practitioner/Actor 7. Authority/Governor ... one individual can occupy several of these roles.
rows.statement: Proposes a minimal seven-role actor taxonomy abstracted from Chapter 4's named characters -- Source/Teacher, Questioner/Learner, Recipient, Transmitter, Custodian, Practitioner/Actor, Authority/Governor -- explicitly noting the person/role distinction: one individual (e.g. Vivasvan = Recipient+Transmitter; Krishna = Source+Teacher+Interpreter) can occupy several roles simultaneously, and this distinction is flagged as important for the later return to KnowledgeOS architecture.

rows.anchor: Chapter 4 gives us three different epistemic relationships: A. Transmission K1 -> K2. B. Questioning Q(K). C. Realization/application K -> Action. So knowledge is not simply: Document -> Document. It is: Knowledge -> Person -> Inquiry -> Understanding -> Action.
rows.statement: Identifies three distinct epistemic relationship types present in Chapter 4 -- Transmission (K1->K2), Questioning (Q(K)), and Realization/application (K->Action) -- and argues this shows knowledge transfer is not a simple Document->Document relation but rather a Knowledge->Person->Inquiry->Understanding->Action chain, offered as a potentially important validation of KnowledgeOS's direction, though the correspondence is explicitly flagged as needing careful testing rather than assumption.
missing: formal proof/test of correspondence to KnowledgeOS pipeline

assumptions.statement: Knowledge has a lineage, and lineage requires Transmission + Reception + Inquiry + Understanding + Application to be meaningful
assumptions.anchor: Knowledge has a lineage. ... Transmission + Reception + Inquiry + Understanding + Application.

rows.anchor: The next thing I would do—before Step 158—is summarize Chapter 4's actual propositions and sequence (roughly verses 4.1-4.42) and then build a Chapter 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 cumulative matrix showing what each chapter added to our architectural lenses.
rows.statement: Plans two follow-on steps before proceeding to 'Step 158': (a) summarize Chapter 4's actual propositions/verse sequence (4.1-4.42), and (b) build a cumulative Chapter 1->2->3->4 matrix of what each chapter added to the architectural lenses, to determine whether Chapter 4 adds a genuinely new architectural principle or merely reinforces prior findings.

rows.anchor: I would not model Krishna simply as "the administrator who has all memory." A better abstraction is: Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity. ... A trusted epistemic authority that can establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.
rows.statement: Rejects modeling Krishna as 'an administrator who has all memory' (an omniscient-database analogy) and instead re-characterizes his architectural role as Witness + Teacher + Source of continuity -- a trusted epistemic authority able to establish continuity across states that individually lack complete historical memory.

rows.anchor: PHASE 3F -- GITA LENS ... Maintain: GITA TEXT -> INTERPRETATION -> STRUCTURAL INSIGHT -> ARCHITECTURAL ANALOGY -> ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE ... Do not claim equivalence between Krishna/Gita concepts and software components unless explicitly justified as an analogy.
rows.statement: Specifies a mandatory five-stage discipline for handling Gita material (Gita Text -> Interpretation -> Structural Insight -> Architectural Analogy -> Architectural Consequence) and forbids asserting equivalence between Krishna/Gita concepts and software components without explicit analogy justification -- the exact discipline followed by the Chapter-4 files (S1066, S1067) elsewhere in this batch.

Phase 3: NOT AUTHORIZED. Book synthesis: NOT AUTHORIZED.

sources.note: Step 204's eight-field canonical transition contract and the invariant-preservation rule, plus the local/global and cross-context invariant-contract distinctions and the restated composability condition.

rows.anchor: Transition= Intent+Precondition+Authority+Evidence+StateChange+InvariantCheck+Lineage. So a domain transition is a semantic operation, not a database operation.
rows.statement: Rejects the naive old-state->UPDATE->new-state model, defining a Transition as a semantic operation composed of Intent, Precondition, Authority, Evidence, StateChange, InvariantCheck, and Lineage.

rows.anchor: T_\tau=(Pre,Input,Authority,Policy,Effect,Post,Invariant,Lineage). ... If these cannot be answered, the transition is architecturally underspecified.
rows.statement: Defines a canonical eight-field transition contract T_tau (Pre, Input, Authority, Policy, Effect, Post, Invariant, Lineage) with eight corresponding mandatory questions; failure to answer any of them marks the transition architecturally underspecified.

rows.anchor: I(s)\land Pre_\tau(s,c) \Rightarrow I(\tau(s,c)). Therefore: ValidTransition \Rightarrow InvariantPreservation.
rows.statement: States the invariant-preservation rule as a mathematical foundation of the architecture constitution: a valid transition, applied to a state already satisfying an invariant, must produce a state that still satisfies it.

rows.anchor: I_local from: I_global. A bounded context should be responsible for its local invariants. ... These should not be implemented as one giant invariant system.
rows.statement: Distinguishes local invariants (owned by one bounded context, e.g. evidence requiring provenance before verification) from global invariants, warning against implementing them as one giant invariant system.

rows.anchor: The Decision Context should not directly reach into the Assessment aggregate's database. Instead we define a contract: AssessmentQualificationContract.
rows.statement: Cross-context invariants (e.g. a Decision requiring Assessment.status=Supported) must be enforced via an explicit named contract (e.g. AssessmentQualificationContract) rather than direct cross-aggregate database access.

rows.anchor: Valid_A(x) \land Satisfies(C_{A\rightarrow B},x) \Rightarrow Accept_B(x). This is a very important DDD principle.
rows.statement: Formalizes contract validity across bounded contexts: an object valid in context A is accepted by context B only if it also satisfies the explicit A-to-B contract, not merely by virtue of being valid in A.

rows.anchor: Composable(\tau_1,\tau_2) \iff Post(\tau_1)\supseteq Pre(\tau_2) ... ProcessValidity= TransitionValidity+ CompositionValidity+ InvariantPreservation.
rows.statement: Restates and consolidates the transition-composability condition from Step 198/200 formally, defining ProcessValidity as the conjunction of TransitionValidity, CompositionValidity, and InvariantPreservation; worked example -- verifying evidence into VerifiedEvidence then into an Assessment composes only if the verification's postcondition satisfies the assessment step's required evidence count.

rows.anchor: PASS (Mathematical) ... PASS (DDD) ... PASS (Statistical) ... PASS (Governance) ... PASS (Epistemic) ... CONSISTENT (Gita lens).
rows.statement: Step 204 gives all-PASS per-discipline verdicts: mathematical (coherent formal transition structure), DDD (aggregate boundaries derivable from consistency requirements, not nouns), statistical (risk/uncertainty representable without confusing probability with policy), governance (authority/policy/decision/execution remain separate), epistemic (observation/evidence/proposition/assessment remain distinct), Gita lens consistent (Context->Identity->Action->Knowledge/Discernment).

rows.anchor: Composition law stated two non-equivalent ways in one paragraph: Post_tau1 => Pre_tau2 and Composable iff Post(tau1) superset-eq Pre(tau2) — (implication and superset run in opposite directions under the states-set reading; unreconciled — candidate L1 finding).
rows.statement: Identifies a genuine internal inconsistency inside this batch's own Step 204 (S1423): the transition composability law is stated two non-equivalent ways in the same paragraph (an implication form and a superset-containment form) which run in opposite directions under a set-theoretic reading of the states involved -- flagged as a candidate finding for future Level-1 formal verification.

lineage_claims.quote: Composition law stated two non-equivalent ways in one paragraph: Post_{τ1} ⇒ Pre_{τ2} and Composable ⟺ Post(τ1) ⊇ Pre(τ2)

rows.anchor: Q13/Q14/Q15/Q20/step-031 never address idempotency, commutativity, compensation, or partial order — the 'frozen' transition model and the transition algebra are disjoint developments with different signatures.

sources.note: Final file in the batch's hpa Gita-kernel thread (chronologically first Gita chapter, read last): treats Chapter 1 (Arjuna's crisis) not as a source of new primitives but as a rich model of the kernel's PATHOLOGICAL/FAILURE state before discrimination operates, motivating Chapter 2's reconstruction. Central pipeline: Observation->Interpretation->Attachment->Conflict->Distortion->Decision Paralysis. Introduces Inspect(K_t,C)->O_{t+1} as a legitimate context-acquisition operator (Arjuna's chariot-positioning request). Gives Observation != Knowledge != Correct Decision. Refines Zero into three forms {Missing information, Missing interpretation, Blocked discrimination}, with Arjuna's case being primarily interpretive/discriminative deficiency despite abundant information. Introduces the model-adequacy concept: a valid inference can still arise from an inadequate model, so the kernel must ask not only InferenceValid? but ModelAdequate?, with M_t--Buddhi-->M_{t+1} as the correction mechanism. Gives Proposition=(Content,Evidence,Context,Time,Provenance) reinforcing the existing Assertion model. Proposes KernelState=(K_t,O_t,C_t,B_t,E_t) contrasting a healthy pipeline with the Arjuna failure pipeline (Observation->Representation->Attachment->Conflicting evaluations->Buddhi overload->Decision paralysis). Reaffirms Krishna != Kernel (Krishna-lens ~ Guidance/Correction function, distinct from Kernel ~ Mind-like processing unit). Concludes with candidate kernel (fraktur M)_t=(O_t,K_t,C_t,P_t,B_t,G_t,D_t) and FIVE fundamental kernel responsibilities: Observe, Represent, Discriminate(Buddhi), Revise, Decide/prepare-for-action -- explicitly not yet promoted to canonical operations, proposing as final next step deriving the minimal operator algebra and testing whether all of Chapters 1-18 can be represented without ad-hoc operators.
The Gita Chapter 1 as kernel pathological/failure-state theory, first proposed in B0054 and substantially extended in B0055 (S2261): K_0 tuple, operator algebra, G1 principle, Zero Z1/Z2 typology.

rows.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Interpretation \rightarrow Attachment \rightarrow Conflict \rightarrow Distortion \rightarrow Decision\ Paralysis
rows.statement: Central pipeline abstracting Arjuna's crisis: Observation -> Interpretation -> Attachment -> Conflict -> Distortion -> Decision Paralysis. Arjuna does not lack observations (battlefield, armies, teachers, relatives); the failure occurs after acquisition. Introduces Inspect(K_t,C)->O_{t+1} as a legitimate context-acquisition operation (from Arjuna's request to position the chariot between the armies) -- explicitly an operation, not a new primitive, given the Step 287 discipline. Notes observed entities immediately carry attached semantic relationships (Entity_i -father-> Arjuna), reinforcing the existing Entity+Relation+Proposition+Context model.

rows.anchor: Zero = \begin{cases}Missing\ information\\Missing\ interpretation\\Blocked\ discrimination\end{cases}
rows.statement: Refines Zero into three forms: Missing information, Missing interpretation, Blocked discrimination. Arjuna's case is classified as primarily interpretive/discriminative deficiency despite having substantial information -- a major refinement of the previous Zero interpretation, since he has abundant data but cannot perceive 'the good that would result' (a discrimination failure, not an information gap).

lineage_claims.quote: This is a major refinement.

rows.anchor: A\ valid\ inference\ can\ still\ arise\ from\ an\ inadequate\ model ... ModelAdequate?
rows.statement: From Arjuna's internally coherent but epistemically inadequate argument (kill relatives -> destroy family -> destroy traditions -> social/religious disorder -> bad consequences -> therefore I should not fight): a valid inference can still arise from an inadequate model, since the premises, weighting and interpretation are insufficiently discriminated. Proposes the kernel must evaluate not only InferenceValid? but also ModelAdequate?, with correction modeled as M_t --Buddhi--> M_{t+1} -- assessed as extremely relevant to AI engineering and as precisely what happens throughout the later Gita dialogue (Chapter 1 as the failure state motivating Chapter 2's reconstruction).

rows.anchor: Proposition = (Content,\ Evidence,\ Context,\ Time,\ Provenance)
rows.statement: From Arjuna citing disciplic-succession/authority for his claimed consequences: reinforces that Proposition should not exist without epistemic context, giving Proposition=(Content, Evidence, Context, Time, Provenance) -- assessed as fitting extremely well with the already-reconstructed Assertion model.

rows.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Representation \rightarrow Attachment \rightarrow Conflicting\ evaluations \rightarrow Buddhi\ overload \rightarrow Decision\ paralysis
rows.statement: Proposes KernelState=(K_t,O_t,C_t,B_t,E_t) [represented knowledge, observations, contextual relations, Buddhi/discrimination condition, epistemic/emotional distortion conditions], contrasting a healthy pipeline (Observation->Representation->Discrimination->Decision) with the Arjuna Chapter-1 failure pipeline (Observation->Representation->Attachment->Conflicting evaluations->Buddhi overload->Decision paralysis). Explicitly declines to introduce Attachment as a primitive, instead representing it as a property of Context or of the evaluation process.

rows.anchor: Kṛṣṇa \neq Kernel ... Kṛṣṇa-lens \approx Guidance/Correction\ function
rows.statement: Preserves the theology/architecture boundary: Krishna != Kernel; rather Krishna-lens ~ Guidance/Correction function, while Kernel ~ Mind-like epistemic processing unit -- explicitly to avoid confusing the theological source with software architecture, even while using the chariot/charioteer configuration (Krishna as Hrishikesa, director of the senses, functioning as charioteer) as an architectural metaphor.

rows.anchor: 1.\ Observe ... 2.\ Represent ... 3.\ Discriminate\;(\text{Buddhi}) ... 4.\ Revise ... 5.\ Decide/prepare\ for\ action
rows.statement: Closing statement of the whole hpa Gita-kernel thread: candidate kernel (fraktur M)_t=(O_t,K_t,C_t,P_t,B_t,G_t,D_t) with transition (fraktur M)_t --Omega--> O_{t+1} --Interpret--> K'_{t+1} --Buddhi--> E_{t+1} --Decision--> D_{t+1}. States the formal research result: a system may possess substantial observations and internally coherent propositions while remaining unable to produce an appropriate decision because its interpretive model and discriminative capacity are compromised -- explicitly independent of accepting the Gita's theology. Concludes with five fundamental kernel responsibilities: Observe, Represent, Discriminate (Buddhi), Revise, Decide/prepare-for-action, with Zero exposing unresolved boundaries and the Krishna/Sarathi lens representing guidance/reorientation rather than a knowledge container -- explicitly NOT yet promoted to canonical operations; final proposed next step is deriving the minimal operator algebra from these five responsibilities and testing whether all of Chapters 1-18 can be represented without ad-hoc operators.

rows.anchor: Chapter 1 does not primarily add another knowledge primitive. It adds the initial pathological state from which the kernel must operate.
rows.statement: Chapter 1 defines the initial kernel state K_0=(O_0,P_0,R_0,V_0,C_0,D_0,U_0) (observations, propositions, relations, values, context, detected gaps, decision state), which is not empty -- Arjuna has abundant information (armies, relatives, teachers, consequences) yet his decision process collapses, giving the finding 'more information does not imply better decision.'

lineage_claims.quote: After revisiting Chapter 1 specifically as the opening state of the whole Gita, I would add it to our KnowledgeOS model

rows.anchor: O\rightarrow P\rightarrow$$ and then evaluates them ... $$P,R,C,V\rightarrow D
rows.statement: Chapter 1 introduces the distinction between observation and interpretation: O->P (observation transformed into interpretation, distorted by attachment/emotion), then P,R,C,V->D (evaluation into decision), giving O != P != D and the pipeline Observation -> Interpretation -> Evaluation -> Decision; observation and knowledge-state construction are not the same operation.

rows.anchor: Knowledge available \land Buddhi impaired \Rightarrow decision failure ... A knowledge system must model not only what is known, but the condition under which known information is being evaluated.
rows.statement: Kernel failure mode: Knowledge available AND Buddhi impaired => decision failure. Arjuna is not information-starved but epistemically overwhelmed and unable to discriminate between competing interpretations and values; a knowledge system must model not only what is known but the condition under which known information is evaluated (connecting to the Sattva/Rajas/Tamas model).
invariants: Knowledge available & Buddhi impaired => decision failure

rows.anchor: Chapter 1 does not give us a new canonical primitive. It gives us something arguably more important: the motivating failure condition of the KnowledgeOS kernel. ... instead of continuing to map individual Gita chapters, we can now attempt to formally specify the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself
rows.statement: Bottom line: Chapter 1 gives no new canonical primitive but the motivating failure condition of the kernel, supporting the pipeline Knowledge State -> Mind/Kernel -> Buddhi -> Discrimination -> Qualification -> Decision -> Action -> new Knowledge State. Proposed next step: stop mapping individual Gita chapters and instead attempt to formally specify the KnowledgeOS Kernel itself (state, Buddhi, modes, operators, invariants, algebra), then test that model against all 18 chapters.

single_candidate_flags.why_uncertain: A 14-category theory-gap taxonomy (Definition/Type/Assumption/Proof/Consistency/Completeness/Identifiability/Measurement/Statistical/Computational/Semantic/Governance/Architecture/Empirical gaps) with a 13-field gap record schema; distinct from the earlier five-member Gap taxonomy (Epistemic/Understanding/Normative/Decision/Domain) -- unclear if this replaces, coexists with, or is unrelated to that object, and whether it matches the corpus's own 'existing G1-G14 taxonomy' the file references as already present.

sources.note: Replaces the three-dimensional discrepancy Δ=(Δ_E,Δ_U,Δ_D) with a five-member Gap taxonomy adding Normative and Decision gaps, and rejects 'Δ=∅ ⇒ Success' in favor of DecisionReady=CriteriaSatisfied.

rows.anchor: Gap = (Epistemic, Understanding, Normative, Decision, Domain)
rows.statement: Extends Δ_U to add Δ_Normative and Δ_Decision, giving Δ=(Δ_E,Δ_U,Δ_N,Δ_D,Δ_Decision), and formalizes a five-member Gap taxonomy: Epistemic (we don't know), Understanding (know facts but not meaning), Normative (don't know what ought to be done), Decision (know facts but can't determine the decision), Domain (reality doesn't match desired state) — 'a major improvement over our earlier three-dimensional discrepancy'. Reworks the Arjuna example's initial discrepancy as Δ_0=(Δ_E,Δ_U,Δ_N,Δ_Decision,Δ_A) (adding affective conflict Δ_A) instead of the earlier (d_Dim,d_Value,d_Epistemic).

lineage_claims.quote: This is a major improvement over our earlier three-dimensional discrepancy.

rows.anchor: Resolution \neq \Delta=\emptyset
rows.statement: Rejects the previous Arjuna example's claim 'After Moral Resolution -> Δ=∅' as a very important correction: even after normative resolution, uncertainty/risk/incomplete domain knowledge/emotional difficulty/consequences may remain, so Resolution ≠ Δ=∅; DecisionReady(Δ,P) may hold even though Δ≠∅. Generalized to abandon 'Δ=∅ ⇒ Success' entirely: DecisionReady=CriteriaSatisfied, not DecisionReady=NoRemainingGaps, so CompleteKnowledge is unnecessary for action — 'a very important property for a real engineering system'.

lineage_claims.target: an earlier Arjuna worked example claiming 'After Moral Resolution → Δ = ∅'
lineage_claims.quote: I would now reject that formulation.

rows.anchor: \Delta = \{ d_1,d_2,\ldots,d_n \}
rows.statement: Retracts freezing the six-dimension discrepancy vector Δ=(Δ_E,Δ_U,Δ_N,Δ_D,Δ_Decision,Δ_A) from S0807, arguing it conflates three different categories (state dimensions, relations, deficiencies) and wrongly assumes orthogonality/separability (a single finding may be simultaneously semantic+normative, or epistemic+decision-relevant). Replaces it with Δ(S,C,P)=Diff(S,Expected(C,P)) yielding a typed SET of findings Δ={d_1,...,d_n} with type(d_i)∈{Epistemic,Semantic,Normative,Domain,Decision,Operational,...}: 'Discrepancy = typed set of findings' judged safer than a fixed vector.

lineage_claims.quote: I would not freeze this yet. ... These are not the same mathematical category.

rows.anchor: Decision = f( Understanding, Norms, Role, Context, Evidence, Options, Criteria )
rows.statement: Demotes Δ_Decision from a first-class discrepancy dimension (proposed in S0807): Decision = f(Understanding,Norms,Role,Context,Evidence,Options,Criteria), with the decision engine instead reporting typed reasons (insufficient evidence, ambiguous norm, conflicting constraints, missing authority, uncertain outcome) rather than a dedicated dimension.

lineage_claims.target: S0807's Δ_Decision as a first-class discrepancy dimension
lineage_claims.quote: I would no longer make: Δ_{Decision} a first-class discrepancy dimension.

rows.anchor: Δ = Diff(CurrentState,ApplicableCriteria)
rows.statement: States explicitly that Chapter 3 does NOT establish KnowledgeOS as a software architecture, nor prove S=(W,K,U,N,A,C), Δ=Diff(S,C), that Zero/Lord/Sārathi must be separate software components, or that discrepancy should be a fixed vector (Δ_E,Δ_U,Δ_N,Δ_D,...) — after the second review the vector is explicitly not frozen, in favor of Δ=Diff(CurrentState,ApplicableCriteria) yielding a typed set of findings rather than a fixed vector.

rows.anchor: UNKNOWN\n    │\n    ├── Dimension unknown
rows.statement: Argues distinguishing kinds of 'I don't know' may be one of the most commercially important capabilities: a ten-item taxonomy — Dimension unknown, Value unknown, Evidence missing, Evidence insufficient, Evidence conflicting, Assertion stale, Context unclear, Assumption unvalidated, Relationship unknown, Consequence unresolved — replacing a collapsed 'I don't know' answer with 'what exactly is the epistemic condition of what we think we know?'.

rows.anchor: \Delta_t = Diff(K_t,I_t)
rows.statement: Δ_t=Diff(K_t,I_t) should be structured (missing dimensions, unknown values, evidence deficiencies, conflicts, temporal issues, context issues, domain deficiencies) rather than a single score, so KnowledgeOS can answer 'how far are we from a state in which this decision can responsibly be made?' — judged more meaningful than an AI confidence score.

rows.anchor: Knowledge Quantity \neq Knowledge Completeness

rows.statement: Formal semantics for ASK[alpha,e] (YES iff e|=K-alpha, else NO) and TELL[alpha,e] (intersect e with the worlds satisfying alpha), and the K operator (K-alpha true at w iff alpha holds in every world w' in the epistemic state e) -- the precise formal machinery underlying the TELL/ASK candidate used loosely elsewhere in this batch.

rows.anchor: (\alpha\supset K\alpha) FALSE ... (K\alpha\supset\alpha) FALSE ... If \models\alpha then \models K\alpha TRUE ... For any subjective sentence sigma: \models(\sigma\supset K\sigma) [positive introspection] ... logical omniscience

sources.note: S0407's explicitly non-architectural falsification-question extraction from Nyaya-sutra pramana theory, tarka, realism and debate theory against a minimal Knowledge Kernel; independently re-derives Nyaya vocabulary already partially indexed under pramana-four-knowledge-sources/tarka-vs-anumana-distinction/hetvabhasa-fallacy-taxonomy/navya-nyaya-relational-ontology (B0006) but frames it as Kernel-boundary falsification questions in the same style as chinese-tarka-audi-kernel-falsification-lens (S0405); references a pre-existing undefined 'anti-reasoner' concept.

rows.anchor: Nyaya treats knowledge as fundamentally relational and process-based, not as a static property of propositions.
rows.statement: Three headline findings from applying Nyaya pramana theory, tarka, realism, and debate theory to the Kernel: (1) knowledge is relational/process-based, not a static property -- a claim is knowledge only if generated by the right kind of process (pramana) and defeasible by legitimate doubt; (2) Nyaya's two-tier epistemology (default trust in cognition vs reflective certification when doubt arises) maps onto a 'knowledge core' (trusted default) vs 'adjudication process' (certification) distinction; (3) Nyaya's theory of error is parasitic on truth (error is misplacement of properties onto the wrong object, requiring prior knowledge of the properties/object), directly relevant to the anti-reasoner concept and the representation-!=-truth problem.

lineage_claims.quote: directly relevant to the anti-reasoner concept and the "representation ≠ truth" problem

rows.anchor: Knowledge Requires Four Factors
rows.statement: Ten Nyaya observations (Part 1): (1) knowledge requires four unified factors -- knower, known, knowledge source, and knowledge itself (Nyaya-sutra 1.1.1); (2) error is parasitic on truth, a misplacement of a property onto the wrong object (Nyaya-sutra 4.2.35, the shell/silver example); (3) a two-tier epistemology of default trust vs certification when doubt arises (2.1.20); (4) pramanas (perception/inference/analogy/testimony, 1.1.3) are causes of veridical cognition, not conscious justifications -- a causal account of knowledge; (5) inference (linga) has a three-part perception->recollection->inference structure (1.1.5); (6) vyapti (invariable concomitance) must be tested in both anvaya (positive) and vyatireka (negative) directions (1.1.34); (7) absence (abhava) requires a counter-correlative (pratiyogi), you cannot assert non-existence of X without knowing what X would be if it existed (4.2.33); (8) perception is defined by four conditions (sense-object connection, language-independence, inerrancy, definitiveness, 1.1.4); (9) the lamp analogy is interpreted as mutual certification among pramanas, not self-certification (2.1.19), a coherentist element within Nyaya's foundationalism; (10) doubt (samsaya) is the catalyst for inquiry, not a failure state, arising from five distinct triggers (1.1.23).

rows.anchor: The 10 Strongest Falsification Questions from Nyaya
rows.statement: Ten falsification questions mirroring the ten observations: definition adequacy (avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava, and whether 'does not depend on language' is even met by a digital system); reason integrity via the five-part pratijna-hetu-udaharana-upanaya-nigamana structure; invariant testing in both anvaya/vyatireka directions; absence-type question for 'retraction'; the five hetvabhasa (pseudo-prover) defects (deviant/contradictory/inconclusive/unproven/mistimed); representation vs truth (viparyaya); whether unknown/doubt/contradiction/error are collapsed into one 'uncertain' state (samsaya); conclusion-excess (nigamana exceeding pratijna+hetu); nigrahasthana argument-integrity checks (proposition/reason changed, meaning shifted); and whether the Kernel distinguishes knowledge by pramana source.

rows.anchor: Knowledge is a Causal Process, Not a Property
rows.statement: Five most-surprising observations: knowledge is generated by a causal process, not possessed as a property (a Kernel might need to track the generation process/pramana, not just the claim); error requires prior knowledge of truth (opposite of the Western default-doubt assumption, so error might be modeled as a modified version of truth, not a separate category); default trust, not skepticism, is Nyaya's epistemic starting point (opposite of the Cartesian default-doubt assumption); absence is a real category with structure (counter-correlative plus type: absolute/prior/subsequent/locus-based); doubt has five distinct causal types, not just confidence degrees.

rows.anchor: The 5 Observations Most Likely Relevant to a Minimal Knowledge Kernel
rows.statement: Five observations ranked most kernel-relevant: the four-factor knower/known/source/knowledge relational structure (a Kernel storing only propositions loses this structure); the two-tier trusted-vs-certified structure; the parasitism thesis (error as modified truth, not a separate category); the counter-correlative requirement for absence/retraction/deletion; the five distinct doubt types (not just a confidence scalar).

rows.anchor: The Debate Framework as Falsification Apparatus
rows.statement: Nyaya's three debate types (vada: truth-seeking debate using pramanas/tarka without tricks; jalpa: disputation using equivocation/misleading objections/clinchers; vitanda: destructive debate refuting without establishing) plus the five-component formal demonstration (proposition/reason/illustration/application/conclusion), five pseudo-provers, and twenty-two clinchers (ways to lose an argument) suggest a Kernel 'argument integrity' test checking definitional defects (avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava), reason defects (savyabhicara/viruddha/satpratipaksa/asiddha/badhita), and argument integrity (proposition/reason/meaning changes).

rows.anchor: 5 Observations That Should NOT Influence Architecture Without Further Evidence
rows.statement: Five Nyaya observations explicitly flagged as not (yet) architecturally actionable: perception-as-inerrant (too specific an epistemological claim); the four metaphysical categories (substance/quality/action/universal); Nyaya's theism (God as causal factor, not relevant to a minimal kernel); the full 22-clincher list (more detail than a minimal kernel needs); Nyaya's realism about universals (jati) as a specific ontological claim.

rows.anchor: Questions That Conventional DDD Analysis May Not Expose
rows.statement: Ten DDD-blind-spot questions: relational (knower/known/source/knowledge) vs identity-holder aggregates; causal generation vs internal justification; error-as-modified-truth vs error-as-separate-category; absence-requires-counter-correlative vs absence-as-non-existence; five doubt types vs a degree-of-uncertainty scalar; knowledge-as-generated-by-causes vs knowledge-as-possession; perception-as-inerrant-by-definition vs perception-as-fallible; testimony-as-inerrant-when-trustworthy vs testimony-as-fallible; definitions tested for avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava vs definition-as-neutral-act; multi-stage (perception/recollection/reflection) vs linear inference.

rows.anchor: These are not questions about missing capabilities. They are questions about the assumptions the Kernel makes about the nature of knowledge itself.
rows.statement: Final consolidated ten architect-facing questions restating the Part 1-2 material: default-trust vs mandatory-certification; error as separate category vs modified truth; knowledge as static property vs dynamic knower/known/source/knowledge relationship; absence types requiring a counter-correlative; five doubt types vs a single uncertainty state; self-testing definitions for avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava; distinguishing the generation process (pramana) from the knowledge itself; representing that generation process per unit of knowledge; self-certifying vs mutually-certifying knowledge sources; retraction as discrete deletion vs gradual correction process.

sources.note: Step 57's dedicated liveness/progress layer: the Enabled⇒◇Completed property (qualified to internal resolution), the terminal-state set and liveness invariant, the four-level liveness hierarchy, temporal governance as domain semantics, the eventual-resolution-not-guaranteed-success reformulation, and the combined KOSContract=(S,L); extends formal-verification-strategy-model's Step-48 safety/liveness distinction into a full standalone calculus with 25 adversarial experiments.

rows.anchor: Liveness formalized: Enabled(D) ⇒ ◇Completed(D); technically-safe-but-operationally-useless warning
rows.statement: Formalizes Safety as for-all t: I(X_t)=True and Liveness as Enabled(D) ⇒ Diamond Completed(D) (an enabled legitimate process eventually reaches its required goal). Example: Decision -> Authorization -> Action can be perfectly safe at every transition while Authorization never happens -- Safety=True but Liveness=False, 'technically safe but operationally useless'. Qualifies the workflow-level liveness goal Valid(W) ⇒ Eventually(Outcome) since the system cannot guarantee an external world event, giving the internally-scoped form: an enabled internal transition ⇒ eventually resolved internal state. Example: if an external Action recipient never responds, KnowledgeOS cannot manufacture Success but must eventually leave Executing via an explicit recovery path (e.g. Executing -> Unknown).

lineage_claims.target: formal-verification-strategy-model's Safety/Liveness distinction (Step 48) and its reference-machine application (Step 56)
lineage_claims.quote: We now test the other half of system correctness.

rows.anchor: Twelve experiments on unbounded internal processes (rejected/unknown authorization, missing evidence, AI/retry loops, human approval, policy/dependency deadlock, starvation) all PASS -- every indefinite wait needs an explicit resolution path
rows.statement: Experiment 1 normal completion (Authorized->Executing->Completed) PASS. Experiment 2 rejected authorization: Waiting->Rejected rather than indefinite WaitingForAuthorization -- PASS. Experiment 3 unknown authorization: Unknown->Escalated rather than indefinite waiting -- PASS, yielding the requirement that every potentially indefinite wait needs an explicit resolution path. Experiment 4 missing evidence: Candidate->EvidenceRequired->{Validated if evidence arrives, Rejected/Expired per policy} rather than endless retry -- PASS. Experiment 5 AI reasoning loop (Proposal_1->Proposal_2->...): bounded by MaxIterations/ReasoningBudget, Loop->Escalated/Unresolved -- PASS, generalizing to the principle that unbounded reasoning (AI agents, statistical optimization, search, rule evaluation, workflow retries) must have a termination condition. Experiment 6 retry loop: RetryCount<=N, Failed->Escalated after N -- PASS, giving 'retry process is finite'; experiment 7 notes exponential backoff t_n=t_0*b^n as an implementation-specific strategy under the domain invariant that retry remains bounded/governed. Experiment 8 human approval: WaitingForHuman->Expired/Escalated after a defined period -- PASS, since human-in-the-loop does not automatically guarantee progress (needs Timeout/Escalation/Delegation). Experiment 9 policy cycle (Policy_A requires Approval_B, Policy_B requires Approval_A, forming A->B->A): a governance deadlock requiring cycle detection over the policy dependency graph -- PASS. Experiment 10 dependency deadlock (Context_A waits for B, B waits for A, forming a wait-for cycle in G=(V,E)): detected as Deadlock -- PASS. Experiment 11 starvation (D0 perpetually deprioritized behind D1,D2,D3,...): requires a fairness mechanism such as WaitingTime(D)<T_max.
invariants: unbounded reasoning/retry/delegation must always have an explicit termination condition

experiment.hypothesis: The liveness model correctly resolves twelve classes of potentially-indefinite internal processes via explicit bounds/escalation rather than allowing indefinite waiting.
experiment.setup: Eleven numbered experiments (57.5-57.20) plus the general termination-condition principle (57.10).
experiment.assumptions: The safety/state-machine model from Steps 51-56 is assumed correctly specified.
experiment.inputs: Eleven scenario premises as summarized in the statement.
experiment.method: For each scenario, check whether the model provides an explicit bounded resolution path rather than allowing indefinite waiting.
experiment.result: All experiments PASS.
experiment.interpretation: Every potentially indefinite wait needs, and can be given, an explicit resolution path (timeout/escalation/expiry/fairness).
experiment.limitations: Manual scenario reasoning, not automated/exhaustive analysis.

rows.anchor: Thirteen further experiments: knowledge-revision oscillation, nonconvergence, non-optimal solvers, distributed partition/CAP, eventual consistency, poison/duplicate events, unavailable providers, temporal expiry, infinite delegation, recursive workflow (all PASS)
rows.statement: Experiment 12 knowledge revision loop (C1->C2->C3->C1 continuously invalidating): needs RevisionHistory and a StabilityCriterion. Statistical convergence: x_{n+1}=f(x_n) requiring |x_{n+1}-x_n|<epsilon or, after N_max, returning Unresolved -- 'failure to converge must be representable as a valid result; the system must not fabricate convergence'. Experiment 13 optimization: a solver may not find the global optimum, recording Status=Approximate or Unresolved, never silently claiming GlobalOptimum -- PASS. Experiment 14 distributed partition (Context_A not<->Context_B): must choose block/bounded-stale-state/degrade/queue/reconcile without silently violating invariants; a CAP-style consequence requires an explicit per-operation Consistency-vs-Availability choice, not a universal system-wide setting, and different bounded contexts may need different consistency (e.g. Audit stronger than Analytics), so ConsistencyPolicy belongs to the context/use case. Experiment 15 eventual consistency (EvidenceRegistered not yet visible in Knowledge Context): a query may return EvidenceUnavailable but must not claim NoEvidenceExists -- PASS, giving NotYetObserved != DoesNotExist as a principle that must survive into query semantics. Experiment 16 duplicate event: idempotent processing keeps state correct, so Duplicate(E) must not destroy liveness -- PASS. Experiment 17 poison event: a repeatedly-failing malformed event must not block the queue (Queue->Retry->Retry->... forever) -- requires DeadLetter/quarantine semantics, giving the principle that a permanently failing message must not block the entire workflow -- PASS. Experiments 18-20 unavailable AI provider / statistical engine / database: each must resolve to an explicit AIUnavailable/Fallback/Unresolved or Unavailable state (never False, never invented state), preserving deterministic domain operation -- all PASS. Experiment 21 expired authorization (t2>AuthorizationValidUntil): execution Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 22 expired evidence (validity window [t0,t1], queried at t>t1): RevalidationRequired -- PASS. Experiment 23 expired model (no longer approved): Rejected or RequiresModelUpdate -- PASS. Experiment 24 infinite agent delegation (A->B->C->A): bounded via DelegationDepth<=N -- PASS. Experiment 25 recursive workflow (W1->W2->W3->...): bounded via RecursionDepth or an explicit termination criterion -- PASS.
invariants: NotYetObserved ≠ DoesNotExist, surviving into query semantics
a permanently failing message must not block the entire workflow
a solver never silently claims GlobalOptimum when only Approximate/Unresolved is justified

experiment.hypothesis: The liveness model correctly resolves thirteen further classes of potentially-indefinite or distributed-uncertainty scenarios via explicit bounded/quarantine/consistency-aware semantics.
experiment.setup: Fourteen numbered experiments (57.21-57.52, including the statistical-convergence discussion at 57.22-57.23).
experiment.assumptions: The safety/state-machine model and the terminal-state semantics from earlier in this file are assumed correctly specified.
experiment.inputs: Fourteen scenario premises as summarized in the statement.
experiment.method: For each scenario, check whether the model provides an explicit bounded/quarantine/consistency-aware resolution rather than silent failure or indefinite blocking.
experiment.result: All experiments PASS.
experiment.interpretation: Distributed uncertainty, provider unavailability, temporal expiry, and unbounded delegation/recursion are all resolvable via explicit governed semantics rather than ad hoc failure.
experiment.limitations: Manual scenario reasoning, not automated/exhaustive analysis.

rows.anchor: Liveness invariant: every reachable nonterminal state has a governed exit path; terminal-state set T; workflow graph reachability
rows.statement: Formulates the general liveness rule: for every workflow state s there must exist a finite path to one of Success, Failure, Rejected, Expired, Escalated, Unresolved -- 'every nonterminal state must have a governed exit path'. States this is stronger-than-naive because success cannot be guaranteed in an open world; instead the guarantee is that no legitimate workflow remains semantically undefined forever. Defines the terminal set T={Completed,Failed,Rejected,Expired,Escalated,Unresolved} and the workflow graph G_W=(V,E), requiring every reachable nonterminal state v to have a path v-leadsto->t for some t in T -- with the qualification that this does not require every external event to eventually arrive; Timeout/Expiry/Escalation provide semantic termination instead.
invariants: I_Liveness: every reachable nonterminal workflow state has a governed termination/resolution path

rows.anchor: Four-level liveness hierarchy: transition, workflow, operational, organizational
rows.statement: Distinguishes four liveness levels that must not be conflated: Level 1 Transition liveness (a valid command eventually resolves); Level 2 Workflow liveness (a valid workflow eventually reaches a terminal state); Level 3 Operational liveness (the deployed system remains capable of processing work); Level 4 Organizational liveness (humans/governance processes actually respond).

rows.anchor: Temporal governance as first-class domain semantics; expiring authorization/evidence/model as domain behavior; Policy=(Rules,ValidityInterval,ResolutionBehavior)
rows.statement: States that liveness introduces Time as a first-class architectural concern (the mathematical architecture is strong on State and Transition but needs explicit Temporal Governance), requiring concepts like Timeout, Deadline, Expiry, RetryLimit, EscalationRule -- 'not merely infrastructure settings when they affect domain semantics'. Example: Authorization(t>t_expiry)=Expired after 24h is domain behavior, not an infrastructure timer. Extends Policy to Policy=(Rules, ValidityInterval, ResolutionBehavior).

rows.anchor: Liveness = eventual resolution, not guaranteed success; KOSContract=(S,L) combining Safety and Liveness contracts
rows.statement: Reformulates the correct liveness guarantee: since ExternalSystemEventuallyResponds cannot be guaranteed, the architecture guarantees Eventually(Resolved), not Eventually(Success) -- 'Liveness = eventual resolution, not guaranteed success'. Combines Safety Box I(X) and Liveness Diamond Terminal into Box I(X) and Diamond Terminal under explicitly defined assumptions (e.g. A1=NetworkEventuallyRecovers; if false, the guarantee weakens to Eventually(Unknown/Unresolved)). Defines a Liveness Contract L=(Timeouts, Deadlines, Retries, Escalation, Termination, Fairness, Recovery) and a Safety contract S=(Invariants, Authorization, Integrity, Consistency, Provenance), combined into KOSContract=(S,L).
invariants: Liveness guarantees eventual resolution, never guaranteed success, for an open system

rows.anchor: Step 57 verdict PASS WITH IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION; opens Step 58 on compositional correctness across bounded contexts
rows.statement: Declares STEP 57 -- PASS WITH IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION: the model supports safety and liveness provided every potentially indefinite process has an explicit timeout, escalation, retry, expiry, or unresolved path. Summarizes the progression Mathematics -> DDD -> Contracts -> Executable State -> Safety -> Liveness. Opens Step 58 (Compositional Correctness): whether independently correct bounded contexts can compose into an incorrect system, formally testing whether I_A ∧ I_B ∧ Contract_AB implies the relevant I_Global -- examining cross-context invariants, contract compatibility, distributed transactions, semantic translation, eventual consistency, race conditions, multi-agent composition, and global provenance, framed as necessary before the mathematical model is 'sufficiently mature for architectural freezing'.

rows.anchor: Circular cross-context dependency detected via a Dependency Graph; feedback loop != deadlock; well-founded progress measure for productive cycles
rows.statement: Constructs a circular context dependency (Decision needs Knowledge needs Evidence needs ExternalSource needs Authorization needs Decision) that is globally impossible despite every local rule being correct; detected as a Cycle -- PASS provided dependency analysis runs before workflow activation, revealing the need for an architecture-level Dependency Graph G_D=(Contexts,Dependencies), where cycles are not automatically invalid but workflow-critical cycles must be explicitly justified. Distinguishes FeedbackLoop != Deadlock: an intentional Learning<->Knowledge or Knowledge->Action->Outcome->Learning->Knowledge cycle is acceptable if there is temporal progression (Version_next>Version_current), whereas a nonproductive cycle (K_t->K_t->K_t with no progression) repeated indefinitely is a Liveness Failure. Introduces a well-founded progress measure mu(X) in W (no infinite descending chain, e.g. RemainingSteps in N) with each transition satisfying mu(X_{t+1})<mu(X_t), proving termination for a given workflow; distinguishes FiniteWorkflow from PersistentProcess (learning may continue indefinitely and needs Progress rather than termination, measured e.g. by new evidence, reduced uncertainty, improved model performance, validated knowledge, resolved conflicts).

rows.anchor: State_{Arjuna} = (K,U,N,D,E)
rows.statement: Arjuna's problem is not purely epistemic: KnowledgeGap+UnderstandingGap+NormativeGap+ActionConflict can occur simultaneously, giving State_Arjuna=(K,U,N,D,E) where E is emotional/psychological state, modeled as a separate AffectiveState rather than folded into the Knowledge State. Suggests a DDD separation of concerns: Inquiry, Knowledge, Understanding, NormativeReasoning, Decision, Action, AffectiveContext as different concerns.

rows.anchor: ActorState = (Role, Capabilities, KnowledgeAccess, Authority, Purpose, Commitments, AffectiveContext)
rows.statement: Formalizes Actor State (Role, Capabilities, KnowledgeAccess, Authority, Purpose, Commitments, AffectiveContext), making Arjuna formally representable and establishing KnowledgeState ≠ ActorState: Action = f(Knowledge, Actor, Role, Purpose, Norms, Authority) — the same Knowledge State can produce different actions for different actors.

rows.anchor: Actor \neq Role \neq Duty
rows.statement: Strengthens Role's centrality (verse 35, own duty vs another's): Duty=f(Role,Context,NormativeFramework) rather than Duty=f(Actor) — a person has duties in a role under a normative context, not directly. Models Actor--holds-->Role--activates-->Duty--constrained by-->Norm as a value-object chain, giving Actor ≠ Role ≠ Duty. Warns against generalizing sva-dharma (embedded in varṇa/āśrama) carelessly into 'every software actor has a role and therefore a duty' — the valid abstraction is narrower: when a normative system assigns responsibilities by role, role-context must participate in determining applicable duties.

rows.statement: Retains a causal chain (Sense Objects->Attachment/Desire->Distortion->Impaired Knowledge->Action, verse 40's lust-covers-knowledge claim) showing AgentState can affect InterpretationOfKnowledge, but corrects S0807's 'AffectiveState' as too narrow, replacing it with a broader AgentCondition (cognitive condition, motivational condition, affective condition, capability, role, authority, commitments), giving Interpretation=f(Knowledge,AgentCondition,Context).
